#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build the full findings report for the technology inventory.

Run (open Microsoft Word first, so the PDF can be exported from the .docx):
    uv run --with python-docx --with pypdfium2 python3 scripts/build_docx.py

This is the analyst's working document - the long one. The one-page executive
summary that gets forwarded is built by scripts/build_exec_summary.py.

Every table is read from clean/*.csv so the document cannot drift from the
data. Prose lives here rather than being parsed out of the HTML report, because
the two formats want different phrasing.

The look comes from ~/DEV/Baylor_Doc_Style, which is measured from
Software_and_Technology_Management_Framework_DRAFT.docx - the house style Eric
chose on 2026-08-30. Do not restyle this file directly; change the module.

House rules from Kenny Boyd's review history still apply:
  - Document status visible on every page. The house style carries it in the
    footer and the meta block rather than a running header.
  - No language implying the department was previously incompetent. Findings
    are written as capability the framework would add, not as failure.
  - Neutral, descriptive labels. Nothing that ranks a unit.
"""

import csv
import os
import subprocess
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/Baylor_Doc_Style")
from baylor_docstyle import BaylorDoc  # noqa: E402

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
CLEAN = os.path.join(ROOT, "clean")
DELIV = os.path.join(ROOT, "deliverables")
STEM = "Tech_Inventory_FINDINGS_ER_2026-08-29"

TITLE = "Athletics Technology Inventory"
DECK = ("Thirty-seven submissions across the department. The finding is not "
        "that there is too much technology — it is that almost none of it is "
        "shared.")
STATUS = "Interim — collection open to 29 September 2026"

PRETTY = {"video-analytics": "Video & analytics", "comms-media": "Comms & media",
          "office-general": "Office general", "equipment-ops": "Equipment ops",
          "athlete-management": "Athlete management", "ai-general": "AI tools",
          "food-travel": "Food & travel", "social-media": "Social media",
          "athlete-stipend": "Athlete stipend", "uncategorised": "Unidentified"}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# data
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def load():
    def rd(name):
        with open(os.path.join(CLEAN, name), encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return list(csv.DictReader(f))

    master = [r for r in rd("tech_master.csv") if r["category"] != "excluded"]
    long = [r for r in rd("tech_inventory_long.csv") if r["category"] != "excluded"]
    return (master, long, rd("coverage.csv"), rd("stopped_using.csv"),
            rd("unmapped_review.csv"))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def main():
    master, long, cov, stopped, unmapped = load()

    n_resp = len({r["response_id"] for r in long}) + 1   # + the prose response
    units_total = len(cov)
    units_in = len([r for r in cov if r["status"] in ("responded", "MULTIPLE")])
    units_out = [r["unit"] for r in cov
                 if r["status"] == "NO RESPONSE" and r["unit"] != "Other"]
    n_products = len(master)
    n_athlete = len([r for r in master if r["athlete_data_likely"] == "Y"])
    n_single = len([r for r in master if int(r["unit_count"]) == 1])
    n_mentions = len(long)

    d = BaylorDoc(TITLE, deck=DECK, status=STATUS)

    d.meta([
        ["Status", "**Interim** — collection stays open to the department "
                   "soft deadline of 29 September 2026"],
        ["Date", "29 August 2026"],
        ["Source", "Microsoft Forms — Quick Inventory (5 questions), "
                   "export of 29 August 2026"],
        ["Prepared by", "Applied Performance, Baylor Athletics"],
        ["Companion", "Athletics Technology Inventory — Executive Summary "
                      "(one page)"],
    ])

    d.callout(
        "Two deadlines, not one",
        "29 August was Applied Performance's own deadline. The all-staff "
        "meeting on 24 August set a department-wide soft deadline of "
        "**29 September**, with unit leaders assigning staff to complete the "
        "survey. Every figure in this document is an interim read at the "
        "earlier date, and the units still to respond have a month to run.")

    # --- 1 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("At a glance — where the inventory stands")
    d.table(
        ["Measure", "Figure", "Note"],
        [["Submissions to date", n_resp,
          "36 listed technology; one was a new hire awaiting equipment"],
         ["Units responding", "{} of {}".format(units_in, units_total),
          "Interim — five units still outstanding, one month to run"],
         ["Distinct products", n_products,
          "Resolved from {} separate mentions".format(n_mentions)],
         ["Products touching athlete data", n_athlete,
          "{}% of the estate, by category — a screening list, not a "
          "confirmed count".format(round(100 * n_athlete / n_products))],

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

query.description: Natural language description of what to find (e.g., "search bar", "add to cart button", "product title containing organic")

tabId.description: Tab ID to search in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

tabId.description: Tab ID to extract text from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool
entries.description: Execute JavaScript code in the context of the current page. The code runs in the page's context and can interact with the DOM, window object, and page variables. Returns the result of the last expression or any thrown errors. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

text.description: The JavaScript code to execute. Evaluated in the page context with REPL semantics: top-level `await` works, and the result of the last expression is returned automatically — write the expression you want (e.g. `window.myData.value`, or `await fetch(url).then(r=>r.json())`) rather than `return ...`. You can access and modify the DOM, call page functions, and interact with page variables.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the code in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
entries.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page
entries.description: Get an accessibility tree representation of elements on the page. By default returns all elements including non-visible ones. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default. If the output exceeds this limit it is truncated at a line boundary, with a note giving the full size — pass a larger max_chars, or use depth/ref_id to focus on part of the page. Optionally filter for only interactive elements. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

filter.description: Filter elements: "interactive" for buttons/links/inputs only, "all" for all elements including non-visible ones (default: all elements)

tabId.description: Tab ID to read from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

depth.description: Maximum depth of the tree to traverse (default: 15). Use a smaller depth if output is too large.

ref_id.description: Reference ID of a parent element to read. Will return the specified element and all its children. Use this to focus on a specific part of the page when output is too large.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters for output (default: 50000). Set to a higher value if your client can handle large outputs.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp
entries.description: Get context information about the current MCP tab group. Returns all tab IDs inside the group if it exists. CRITICAL: You must get the context at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Each new conversation should create its own new tab (using tabs_create_mcp) rather than reusing existing tabs, unless the user explicitly asks to use an existing tab.

createIfEmpty.description: Creates a new MCP tab group if none exists, creates a new Window with a new tab group containing an empty tab (which can be used for this conversation). If a MCP tab group already exists, this parameter has no effect.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
entries.description: Creates a new empty tab in the MCP tab group. CRITICAL: You must get the context using tabs_context_mcp at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Tabs you create are yours to clean up: close each one with tabs_close_mcp as soon as you no longer need it, and close any that remain before finishing your task. Leave a tab open only if the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

# Athletics Technology Inventory — Findings

**Date:** 2026-08-29
**Status:** Interim. Applied Performance's own deadline was 29 August; the
department-wide soft deadline set at the 24 August all-staff meeting is
**29 September**, so collection is still open.
**Source:** `raw/Quick_Inventory_export_2026-08-29.xlsx` — export taken 29 August,
37 submissions (the earlier 2026-08-24 export had 15 and is kept in `raw/` for
comparison)
**Pipeline:** `scripts/clean_inventory.py` + `scripts/aliases.py` → `clean/*.csv`

---

## 1. Coverage

**37 submissions. 36 listed technology** — one was prose from a new hire who has
not received a laptop yet. **27 units responded** out of 33 on the list.

**6 had not responded as of 29 August:**

Golf (M) · Tennis (M) · Tennis (W) · Volleyball · Business Office · Other

One of those six is not a real gap: **"Other"** was never used by anyone and looks
like it was dropped from the live form once real units were added.

("Marketing and Fan Experience" is confirmed by Eric as what the Marketing
department is now called. The two are merged, so Marketing counts as having
responded.)

**So five units are still outstanding: Golf (M), Tennis (M), Tennis (W),
Volleyball, and the Business Office.** That is roughly **85% coverage with a month
still to run.** The Business Office is the one worth a direct ask — it holds the
contract records this inventory is designed to be read against.

Eight units submitted more than once: Football (3), Athletic Medicine (3), Baseball,
Basketball (M), Basketball (W), Track & Field / Cross Country, Athletic Mental Health
Services, Communications (2 each). These are different people describing different
slices of the same unit, so they were kept and tagged, not merged.

> **The unit list is not the one in the spec.** The Google Form spec lists 26
> options. The live Microsoft Form clearly differs — it produced answers like
> "Brand Engagement", "Spirit (Cheer, Dance, Mascots)", "Student Athlete Formation",
> "External/Revenue/Ticketing", "Equipment", "Broadcast and Big Screens" and
> "Development", none of which are on the spec's list. It also spells two units
> differently ("Track and Field/Cross Country", "Acrobatics and Tumbling"). Those
> spellings are now normalised, so both units correctly count as having responded.
> The working list is 33 units. Confirm it against the live form.

---

## 2. What is in the building

- **310 technology mentions**, resolving to **147 distinct products.**
  (14 further fragments were respondent section headers, sentence pieces, or
  physical equipment like helmets and jerseys. Those are tagged `excluded`, not
  counted.)
- **60 of 147 (41%) plausibly touch student-athlete information** — performance,
  medical, athlete-management, video-analytics, recruiting, academic, or the
  athlete meal-money stipend.
- **110 of 147 (75%) were named by exactly one unit.** Only 37 products are shared.

By category:

| Category | Distinct products |
|---|---|
| video-analytics | 19 |
| comms-media | 16 |
| performance | 15 |
| admin | 14 |
| broadcast | 13 |
| productivity | 12 |
| medical | 10 |
| office-general | 6 |
| recruiting | 6 |
| hardware | 5 |
| equipment-ops | 5 |
| academic | 5 |
| athlete-management | 4 |
| ai-general | 4 |
| facility | 4 |
| ticketing | 3 |
| food-travel | 2 |
| athlete-stipend | 1 |
| social-media | 1 |
| unidentified | 2 |

---

## 3. The long tail is the story

Three quarters of the software in this department is used by exactly one unit.
That is the population no central process is watching, and it is where surprises
live. Concretely, it includes AI tools nobody approved centrally (Claude, ChatGPT,
Gemini, Microsoft Copilot), a scatter of productivity apps (Notion, Asana, Todoist,
Padlet, Sling, GroupMe, WhatsApp, TeamUp), and one-off athlete-facing systems
(Nix Biosensors, Calera CORE, Boost Treadmills, C3 Logix, XO Armor, Hologic DXA).

Only a handful of platforms are genuinely departmental:

| Product | Units | Category |
|---|---|---|
| Teamworks | 12 | athlete-management |
| Microsoft Office | 11 | office-general |
| Adobe Creative Suite | 7 | office-general |
| Catapult | 6 | performance |
| Kitman Labs | 6 | athlete-management |
| VALD | 6 | performance |
| Box | 5 | admin |
| Canva | 5 | comms-media |
| Microsoft Teams | 4 | productivity |
| Greenfly | 3 | comms-media |
| Kinexon | 3 | performance |
| Perch | 3 | performance |
| Trackman | 3 | performance |

**Teamworks at 12 units is the only thing close to a department-wide system.**

---

## 4. Overlapping athlete-monitoring vendors

Athlete tracking runs on **Catapult (6 units), Kinexon (3), Polar (1)** with
**Firstbeat** arriving. Force and speed testing runs on **VALD (6), Perch (3),
GymAware, TMG**. Athlete management runs on **Teamworks (12), Kitman Labs (6)**
and **XPS Network**, which overlap heavily in function.

This is the consolidation conversation, and it is now answerable with real numbers
rather than estimates.

---

## 5. Polar is retired by two units and still running in a third

- **Athletics Performance** stopped using Polar Team Pro.
- **Basketball (W)** stopped using Polar Team Pro.
- **Basketball (M)** lists Polar as currently in use.

Surfacing that automatically, and confirming what a vendor retains when a unit
stops using a product, are two capabilities the framework would add. Whether the
retiring units' athlete data was deleted, exported, or is still held by the vendor
is **not answerable from this form.**

---

## 6. Stopped in the last 12 months

| Unit | Product | Vendor still holds data? |
|---|---|---|
| Athletics Performance | Polar Team Pro | Not asked |
| Basketball (W) | Polar Team Pro | Not asked |
| Athletic Medicine | Polaris GPS | Not asked |
| Communications | StatCrew | Not asked |
| Softball | YakkerTech | Not asked |
| Soccer | Hudl Focus | Not asked |
| Performance Nutrition | TikTok and X accounts | Not asked |

**Seven retirements, no recorded data disposition.** The short form did not ask,
so the answer simply is not captured anywhere yet. Confirming what each vendor
retained is the most concrete, closeable action in this dataset.

---

## 7. Coming online

- **Softball** — Trackman, about to be installed.
- **Athletics Performance** — Firstbeat, purchased, not yet in use.

Neither can be confirmed as having gone through a documented vetting step, because
the Quick form did not ask.

---

## 8. One respondent answered the real question unprompted

Broadcast and Big Screens opened their answer with:

> "Everything we have has gone through ITS approval, so they have the list already."

Then listed roughly 13 vendors — Ross Video, Evertz, Grass Valley, Calrec, Adder,
EditShare, Riedel, Daktronics, ANC, Haivision, Vyvx, LTN, Switch. Worth checking
against the ITS IDEA form history: if their list matches, that is a working
baseline for what compliance looks like. If it does not, the "ITS has the list
already" assumption is itself a finding.

---

## What this data still cannot answer

The Quick form has 5 questions. These were never asked, so the framework's planned
flags cannot be produced:

- Does it involve student-athlete information, and what kind?
- How is it paid for, and when does the contract end?
- **Did it go through the ITS IDEA form?** — the bypass-rate number
- Does the vendor still hold data from discontinued products?

The `athlete_data_likely` column is **my category inference, not a respondent
answer.** Treat it as a screening list, not a finding.

---

## Recommended next steps

1. **Follow up with five units before 29 September:** Golf (M), Tennis (M),
   Tennis (W), Volleyball, and the Business Office.
2. **Close the Polar loop.** Two units retired it, a third still runs it, and no
   one knows what the vendor kept. Small, concrete, demonstrable.
3. **Run the Detailed 17-question form as a second pass**, aimed at the 60
   athlete-data candidates in `clean/tech_master.csv`. This analysis produces that
   target list.
4. **Ask ITS for the IDEA form history** and diff it against
   `clean/tech_master.csv`. That gives the bypass number the framework needs, from
   two independent sources rather than a survey question.
5. **Decide on the long tail.** 110 single-unit products is a policy question, not
   a data question.

---

## Judgement calls worth a human eye

See the `review_note` column in `clean/tech_master.csv`:

- **Hudl** — merged "HUDL Statsbomb", "HUDL WyScout" and "HUDL Focus". Same vendor,
  three products. This is why Soccer shows as both using and having stopped Hudl.
- **Whistle** — one unit wrote "Whistle (DataViz)", others wrote bare "DataViz" and
  "GPS DataViz". Assumed to be the same thing.
- **Teamworks** — "TW Nutrition" and "Teamworks Hub" folded in as modules.
- **6-4-3 Charts** — merged Baseball's "643 Charts" and Softball's "6-4-3".
- **Social Media Platforms** — Instagram, TikTok, X and "social media apps
  primarily" bucketed together.
- **Evertz** — the broadcast answer was one run-on list. Only "Routing (Magnum)"
  and "replay (Dreamcatcher)" are read as Evertz; the rest are mapped to their own
  vendors.

- **Red Card** — identified by Eric as the student-athlete meal-money stipend,
  redeemable at selected local vendors. It carries athlete identity and
  transaction records, so it is categorised as athlete data and belongs in the
  detailed second pass even though it is not a performance system.

**Two products could not be identified at all** and are sitting in
`clean/unmapped_review.csv`: **SCRL app** and **JABA**, both named by Brand
Engagement. Eric is checking what they are.

Every other name mapping is explicit in `scripts/aliases.py`. Nothing was guessed
silently.

is **not answerable from this form.**

---

## 6. Stopped in the last 12 months

| Unit | Product | Vendor still holds data? |
|---|---|---|
| Athletics Performance | Polar Team Pro | Not asked |
| Basketball (W) | Polar Team Pro | Not asked |
| Athletic Medicine | Polaris GPS | Not asked |
| Communications | StatCrew | Not asked |
| Softball | YakkerTech | Not asked |
| Soccer | Hudl Focus | Not asked |
| Performance Nutrition | TikTok and X accounts | Not asked |

**Seven retirements, no recorded data disposition.** The short form did not ask,
so the answer simply is not captured anywhere yet. Confirming what each vendor
retained is the most concrete, closeable action in this dataset.

---

## 7. Coming online

- **Softball** — Trackman, about to be installed.
- **Athletics Performance** — Firstbeat, purchased, not yet in use.

Neither can be confirmed as having gone through a documented vetting step, because
the Quick form did not ask.

---

## 8. One respondent answered the real question unprompted

Broadcast and Big Screens opened their answer with:

> "Everything we have has gone through ITS approval, so they have the list already."

Then listed roughly 13 vendors — Ross Video, Evertz, Grass Valley, Calrec, Adder,
EditShare, Riedel, Daktronics, ANC, Haivision, Vyvx, LTN, Switch. Worth checking
against the ITS IDEA form history: if their list matches, that is a working
baseline for what compliance looks like. If it does not, the "ITS has the list
already" assumption is itself a finding.

---

## What this data still cannot answer

The Quick form has 5 questions. These were never asked, so the framework's planned
flags cannot be produced:

- Does it involve student-athlete information, and what kind?
- How is it paid for, and when does the contract end?
- **Did it go through the ITS IDEA form?** — the bypass-rate number
- Does the vendor still hold data from discontinued products?

The `athlete_data_likely` column is **my category inference, not a respondent
answer.** Treat it as a screening list, not a finding.

---

## Recommended next steps

1. **Follow up with five units before 29 September:** Golf (M), Tennis (M),
   Tennis (W), Volleyball, and the Business Office.
2. **Close the Polar loop.** Two units retired it, a third still runs it, and no
   one knows what the vendor kept. Small, concrete, demonstrable.
3. **Run the Detailed 17-question form as a second pass**, aimed at the 60
   athlete-data candidates in `clean/tech_master.csv`. This analysis produces that
   target list.
4. **Ask ITS for the IDEA form history** and diff it against
   `clean/tech_master.csv`. That gives the bypass number the framework needs, from
   two independent sources rather than a survey question.
5. **Decide on the long tail.** 110 single-unit products is a policy question, not
   a data question.

---

## Judgement calls worth a human eye

See the `review_note` column in `clean/tech_master.csv`:

- **Hudl** — merged "HUDL Statsbomb", "HUDL WyScout" and "HUDL Focus". Same vendor,
  three products. This is why Soccer shows as both using and having stopped Hudl.
- **Whistle** — one unit wrote "Whistle (DataViz)", others wrote bare "DataViz" and
  "GPS DataViz". Assumed to be the same thing.
- **Teamworks** — "TW Nutrition" and "Teamworks Hub" folded in as modules.
- **6-4-3 Charts** — merged Baseball's "643 Charts" and Softball's "6-4-3".
- **Social Media Platforms** — Instagram, TikTok, X and "social media apps
  primarily" bucketed together.
- **Evertz** — the broadcast answer was one run-on list. Only "Routing (Magnum)"
  and "replay (Dreamcatcher)" are read as Evertz; the rest are mapped to their own
  vendors.

- **Red Card** — identified by Eric as the student-athlete meal-money stipend,
  redeemable at selected local vendors. It carries athlete identity and
  transaction records, so it is categorised as athlete data and belongs in the
  detailed second pass even though it is not a performance system.

**Two products could not be identified at all** and are sitting in
`clean/unmapped_review.csv`: **SCRL app** and **JABA**, both named by Brand
Engagement. Eric is checking what they are.

Every other name mapping is explicit in `scripts/aliases.py`. Nothing was guessed
silently.

"""Build the full findings report for the technology inventory.

Run (open Microsoft Word first, so the PDF can be exported from the .docx):
    uv run --with python-docx --with pypdfium2 python3 scripts/build_docx.py

This is the analyst's working document - the long one. The one-page executive
summary that gets forwarded is built by scripts/build_exec_summary.py.

Every table is read from clean/*.csv so the document cannot drift from the
data. Prose lives here rather than being parsed out of the HTML report, because
the two formats want different phrasing.

The look comes from ~/DEV/Baylor_Doc_Style, which is measured from
Software_and_Technology_Management_Framework_DRAFT.docx - the house style Eric
chose on 2026-08-30. Do not restyle this file directly; change the module.

    footer and the meta block rather than a running header.
  - No language implying the department was previously incompetent. Findings
    are written as capability the framework would add, not as failure.
  - Neutral, descriptive labels. Nothing that ranks a unit.
"""

import csv
import os
import subprocess
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/Baylor_Doc_Style")
from baylor_docstyle import BaylorDoc  # noqa: E402

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
CLEAN = os.path.join(ROOT, "clean")
DELIV = os.path.join(ROOT, "deliverables")
STEM = "Tech_Inventory_FINDINGS_ER_2026-08-29"

TITLE = "Athletics Technology Inventory"
DECK = ("Thirty-seven submissions across the department. The finding is not "
        "that there is too much technology — it is that almost none of it is "
        "shared.")
STATUS = "Interim — collection open to 29 September 2026"

PRETTY = {"video-analytics": "Video & analytics", "comms-media": "Comms & media",
          "office-general": "Office general", "equipment-ops": "Equipment ops",
          "athlete-management": "Athlete management", "ai-general": "AI tools",
          "food-travel": "Food & travel", "social-media": "Social media",
          "athlete-stipend": "Athlete stipend", "uncategorised": "Unidentified"}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# data
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def load():
    def rd(name):
        with open(os.path.join(CLEAN, name), encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return list(csv.DictReader(f))

    master = [r for r in rd("tech_master.csv") if r["category"] != "excluded"]
    long = [r for r in rd("tech_inventory_long.csv") if r["category"] != "excluded"]

            rd("unmapped_review.csv"))

    tell application "Microsoft Word"
      open POSIX file "{docx}"
      set d to active document
      set n to (compute statistics d statistic statistic pages)
      save as d file name POSIX file "{pdf}" file format format PDF
      close d saving no
      return n
    end tell
    '''.format(docx=docx_path, pdf=pdf_path)
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(["osascript", "-e", script],

    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return None
    if r.returncode != 0:
        return None
    try:
        return int(r.stdout.strip())
    except ValueError:
        return None


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def chrome_pdf(html_path, pdf_path):
    chrome = "/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome"
    subprocess.run(
        [chrome, "--headless", "--disable-gpu", "--no-pdf-header-footer",
         "--print-to-pdf=" + pdf_path, "file://" + html_path],
        check=True, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
    return pdf_path


def word_pdf(docx_path, pdf_path):
    """Export through Word and ask it how many pages it laid out.

    Word is the authority: it is what the reader opens, and its layout is
    measurably taller than the twin's. Returns the page count, or None when
    Word cannot be driven - it blocks on a dialog if the app is not already
    open, so this is best-effort by design.
    """
    script = '''
    tell application "Microsoft Word"
      open POSIX file "{docx}"
      set d to active document
      set n to (compute statistics d statistic statistic pages)
      save as d file name POSIX file "{pdf}" file format format PDF
      close d saving no
      return n
    end tell
    '''.format(docx=docx_path, pdf=pdf_path)
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(["osascript", "-e", script],
                           capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=90)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return None
    if r.returncode != 0:
        return None
    try:
        return int(r.stdout.strip())
    except ValueError:
        return None


def page_count(pdf_path):
    import pypdfium2 as pdfium
    return len(pdfium.PdfDocument(pdf_path))


def main():
    c = content(figures())

    docx_path = os.path.join(DELIV, STEM + ".docx")
    html_path = os.path.join(DELIV, STEM + ".html")
    pdf_path = os.path.join(DELIV, STEM + ".pdf")

    render_docx(c, docx_path)
    print("wrote", docx_path)
    render_html(c, html_path)

    n = word_pdf(docx_path, pdf_path)
    if n is not None:
        source = "Word"
        print("wrote", pdf_path, "(from Word) ->", n, "page(s)")
    else:
        chrome_pdf(html_path, pdf_path)
        n = page_count(pdf_path)
        source = "the HTML twin"
        print("wrote", pdf_path, "(from the HTML twin) ->", n, "page(s)")
        print("[warn] Word did not answer, so this page count is the twin's, "
              "not Word's. Open Microsoft Word and re-run to confirm.")

    if n != 1:
        sys.exit("[error] the executive summary must fit one page; {} laid out "
                 "{}. Cut a checklist row or a bullet.".format(source, n))
    print("one page confirmed by", source)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Claude in Chrome browser automation

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

## Loading deferred tools

If the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load every tool you expect to need in ONE ToolSearch call — the select query accepts a comma-separated list — never one call per tool. Start with the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.

## GIF recording

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:
* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback
* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., "login_process.gif")

## Console log debugging

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:
1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it
2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available

def main():
    master, long, cov, stopped, unmapped = load()

    n_resp = len({r["response_id"] for r in long}) + 1   # + the prose response
    units_total = len(cov)
    units_in = len([r for r in cov if r["status"] in ("responded", "MULTIPLE")])
    units_out = [r["unit"] for r in cov
                 if r["status"] == "NO RESPONSE" and r["unit"] != "Other"]
    n_products = len(master)
    n_athlete = len([r for r in master if r["athlete_data_likely"] == "Y"])
    n_single = len([r for r in master if int(r["unit_count"]) == 1])
    n_mentions = len(long)

    d = BaylorDoc(TITLE, deck=DECK, status=STATUS)

    d.meta([
        ["Status", "**Interim** — collection stays open to the department "
                   "soft deadline of 29 September 2026"],
        ["Date", "29 August 2026"],
        ["Source", "Microsoft Forms — Quick Inventory (5 questions), "
                   "export of 29 August 2026"],
        ["Prepared by", "Applied Performance, Baylor Athletics"],
        ["Companion", "Athletics Technology Inventory — Executive Summary "
                      "(one page)"],
    ])

    d.callout(
        "Two deadlines, not one",
        "29 August was Applied Performance's own deadline. The all-staff "
        "meeting on 24 August set a department-wide soft deadline of "
        "**29 September**, with unit leaders assigning staff to complete the "
        "survey. Every figure in this document is an interim read at the "
        "earlier date, and the units still to respond have a month to run.")

    # --- 1 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("At a glance — where the inventory stands")
    d.table(
        ["Measure", "Figure", "Note"],
        [["Submissions to date", n_resp,
          "36 listed technology; one was a new hire awaiting equipment"],
         ["Units responding", "{} of {}".format(units_in, units_total),
          "Interim — five units still outstanding, one month to run"],
         ["Distinct products", n_products,
          "Resolved from {} separate mentions".format(n_mentions)],
         ["Products touching athlete data", n_athlete,
          "{}% of the estate, by category — a screening list, not a "

"""What the two document builders need from the machine they run on.

Both Eric's machines build these documents: the MacBook (~/DEV) and the Baylor
Windows laptop (~/Desktop/DEV). Everything platform-specific lives here so the
builders stay about the document.

  add_doc_style_to_path()  finds ~/DEV/Baylor_Doc_Style on either machine
  export_date()            the date stamp of the newest raw/ export
  word_pdf()               PDF + page count from Word itself
  chrome_path()            headless Chrome, for the exec summary's HTML twin
"""

import datetime
import glob
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))


def add_doc_style_to_path():
    # Not a sibling of ROOT: inside a .claude/worktrees/ checkout there is none.
    home = os.path.expanduser("~")
    for c in (os.environ.get("BAYLOR_DOC_STYLE"),
              os.path.join(home, "DEV", "Baylor_Doc_Style"),
              os.path.join(home, "Desktop", "DEV", "Baylor_Doc_Style")):
        if c and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(c, "baylor_docstyle.py")):
            sys.path.insert(0, c)
            return c
    sys.exit("[error] Baylor_Doc_Style not found. Set BAYLOR_DOC_STYLE to its folder.")


def export_date():
    """Date of the newest raw export - the same file clean_inventory.py reads."""
    files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, "raw", "Quick_Inventory_export_*.xlsx")))
    if not files:
        sys.exit("[error] no raw/Quick_Inventory_export_*.xlsx found")
    m = re.search(r"(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})", os.path.basename(files[-1]))
    return datetime.date.fromisoformat(m.group(1))


def long_date(d):
    """29 August 2026 - the house date style."""
    return "{} {}".format(d.day, d.strftime("%B %Y"))


def word_pdf(docx_path, pdf_path, timeout=180):
    """Export the PDF through Word and return Word's page count.

    Word is the authority: it is what the reader opens. None means Word could
    not be driven and the PDF was not refreshed.
    """
    docx_path, pdf_path = os.path.abspath(docx_path), os.path.abspath(pdf_path)
    if sys.platform == "darwin":
        # Word blocks on an invisible dialog if the app is not already open.
        cmd = ["osascript", "-e", '''
        tell application "Microsoft Word"
          open POSIX file "{docx}"
          set d to active document
          set n to (compute statistics d statistic statistic pages)
          save as d file name POSIX file "{pdf}" file format format PDF
          close d saving no
          return n
        end tell
        '''.format(docx=docx_path, pdf=pdf_path)]
        env = None
    elif sys.platform == "win32":
        # COM needs no open Word window. If Eric already has Word running, COM
        # attaches to it, so only quit when this build's document was the last.
        cmd = ["powershell.exe", "-NoProfile", "-NonInteractive", "-Command", r'''
        $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
        $w = New-Object -ComObject Word.Application
        $w.DisplayAlerts = 0
        $d = $w.Documents.Open($env:BUILD_DOCX, $false, $true)
        $n = $d.ComputeStatistics(2)
        $d.ExportAsFixedFormat($env:BUILD_PDF, 17)
        $d.Close(0)
        if ($w.Documents.Count -eq 0) { $w.Quit() }
        Write-Output $n
        ''']
        env = dict(os.environ, BUILD_DOCX=docx_path, BUILD_PDF=pdf_path)
    else:
        return None
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True,
                           timeout=timeout, env=env)
    except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, FileNotFoundError):
        return None
    if r.returncode != 0:
        return None
    try:
        return int(r.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1])
    except (ValueError, IndexError):
        return None


def chrome_path():
    for c in ("/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome",
              os.path.join(os.environ.get("PROGRAMFILES", ""), "Google", "Chrome",
                           "Application", "chrome.exe"),
              os.path.join(os.environ.get("LOCALAPPDATA", ""), "Google", "Chrome",
                           "Application", "chrome.exe")):
        if c and os.path.isfile(c):
            return c
    sys.exit("[error] Google Chrome not found for the HTML-twin PDF")
EOF

    ws = openpyxl.load_workbook(p).active   # not read_only: Forms declares A1:A1
    rows = list(ws.iter_rows(values_only=True))
    hdr = [str(h) for h in rows[0]]
    return hdr, [dict(zip(hdr, r)) for r in rows[1:] if any(v is not None for v in r)]


oh, old = load(OLD)
nh, new = load(NEW)

added = [r for r in new if r["ID"] not in oid]

cut = datetime.datetime(2026, 8, 29, 23, 59)
lm = [h for h in nh if "last modified" in h.lower()]
if lm:

           for r in new if r["ID"] in oid and r != old_by[r["ID"]]]
print("pre-existing rows whose content differs (ID, columns):", changed)

"""Response-level delta between the 08-29 export and the new one. Prints no names or emails."""
import datetime
import hashlib
import openpyxl

OLD = "raw/Quick_Inventory_export_2026-08-29.xlsx"
NEW = "raw/Quick_Inventory_export_2026-09-15.xlsx"

for p in (OLD, NEW):
    print(hashlib.md5(open(p, "rb").read()).hexdigest(), p)


def load(p):
    ws = openpyxl.load_workbook(p).active   # not read_only: Forms declares A1:A1
    rows = list(ws.iter_rows(values_only=True))
    hdr = [str(h) for h in rows[0]]
    return hdr, [dict(zip(hdr, r)) for r in rows[1:] if any(v is not None for v in r)]


oh, old = load(OLD)
nh, new = load(NEW)
print("headers equal:", oh == nh)
if oh != nh:
    print("old headers:", oh)
    print("new headers:", nh)
unit = next(h for h in nh if "unit" in h.lower())
role = next((h for h in nh if "role" in h.lower()), None)
print("responses: old", len(old), "new", len(new))

oid = {r["ID"] for r in old}
nid = {r["ID"] for r in new}
print("dropped IDs:", sorted(oid - nid))
added = [r for r in new if r["ID"] not in oid]
print("added responses:", len(added))
for r in added:
    print("  ", r["ID"], str(r["Completion time"])[:16], "|", r[unit],
          "| role:", r.get(role) if role else "")

cut = datetime.datetime(2026, 8, 29, 23, 59)
lm = [h for h in nh if "last modified" in h.lower()]
if lm:
    ed = [(r["ID"], r[unit]) for r in new if r["ID"] in oid
          and isinstance(r[lm[0]], datetime.datetime) and r[lm[0]] > cut]
    print("pre-existing responses modified after 08-29:", ed)
old_by = {r["ID"]: r for r in old}
changed = [(r["ID"], [k for k in nh if r.get(k) != old_by[r["ID"]].get(k)])
           for r in new if r["ID"] in oid and r != old_by[r["ID"]]]
print("pre-existing rows whose content differs (ID, columns):", changed)

"""Response-level delta between the 08-29 export and the new one.

IDs are NOT stable: the Forms-synced workbook renumbers rows, so responses are
matched on (Start time, Completion time). Prints no names or emails; respondents
are shown as R1, R2... by first appearance.
"""
import datetime
import hashlib
import openpyxl

OLD = "raw/Quick_Inventory_export_2026-08-29.xlsx"
NEW = "raw/Quick_Inventory_export_2026-09-15.xlsx"

for p in (OLD, NEW):
    print(hashlib.md5(open(p, "rb").read()).hexdigest(), p)


def load(p):
    ws = openpyxl.load_workbook(p).active   # not read_only: Forms declares A1:A1
    rows = list(ws.iter_rows(values_only=True))
    hdr = [str(h) for h in rows[0]]
    return hdr, [dict(zip(hdr, r)) for r in rows[1:] if any(v is not None for v in r)]


def minute(v):
    if isinstance(v, datetime.datetime):
        return v.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
    return str(v)[:16]


def key(r):
    return (minute(r["Start time"]), minute(r["Completion time"]))


oh, old = load(OLD)
nh, new = load(NEW)
unit = next(h for h in nh if "unit" in h.lower())
role = next(h for h in nh if "role" in h.lower())
using = next(h for h in nh if "currently using" in h.lower())
stopped = next(h for h in nh if "stopped using" in h.lower())
email = next(h for h in nh if h.lower() == "email")
idcol = next(h for h in nh if h.lower() == "id")
print("responses: old", len(old), "new", len(new))

okeys = {key(r): r for r in old}
nkeys = {key(r): r for r in new}
print("old responses missing from new file:",
      [(k, okeys[k][unit]) for k in okeys if k not in nkeys])

cmp_cols = [unit, role, using, stopped]
edited = [(nkeys[k][idcol], nkeys[k][unit],
           [c.split()[0] for c in cmp_cols if (okeys[k].get(c) or "") != (nkeys[k].get(c) or "")])
          for k in okeys if k in nkeys
          and any((okeys[k].get(c) or "") != (nkeys[k].get(c) or "") for c in cmp_cols)]
print("matched responses whose answers changed (new Id, unit, columns):", edited)

added = [r for r in new if key(r) not in okeys]
anon = {}
for r in new:
    anon.setdefault((r[email] or "").lower(), "R{}".format(len(anon) + 1))
print("\nadded responses:", len(added))
for r in sorted(added, key=lambda r: minute(r["Completion time"])):
    print("  Id {:>2} | {} | {:<4} | role: {:<40} | unit: {}".format(
        r[idcol], minute(r["Completion time"]), anon[(r[email] or "").lower()],
        str(r[role])[:40], r[unit]))

by = {}
for r in added:
    by.setdefault(anon[(r[email] or "").lower()], []).append(r[unit])
print("\nadded responses per respondent:")
for a, units in sorted(by.items(), key=lambda x: -len(x[1])):
    print("  {:<4} {:>2}  {}".format(a, len(units), ", ".join(units)))

"""Response-level delta between the 08-29 export and the new one. Prints no names or emails."""
import datetime
import hashlib
import openpyxl

OLD = "raw/Quick_Inventory_export_2026-08-29.xlsx"
NEW = "raw/Quick_Inventory_export_2026-09-15.xlsx"

for p in (OLD, NEW):
    print(hashlib.md5(open(p, "rb").read()).hexdigest(), p)


def load(p):
    ws = openpyxl.load_workbook(p).active   # not read_only: Forms declares A1:A1
    rows = list(ws.iter_rows(values_only=True))
    hdr = [str(h) for h in rows[0]]
    return hdr, [dict(zip(hdr, r)) for r in rows[1:] if any(v is not None for v in r)]


oh, old = load(OLD)
nh, new = load(NEW)
# The Forms-synced workbook heads the column "Id"; the Forms download heads it "ID".
for rows in (old, new):
    for r in rows:
        r["ID"] = r.get("ID", r.get("Id"))
        r.pop("Id", None)
nh = ["ID" if h == "Id" else h for h in nh]
print("headers equal:", oh == nh)
if oh != nh:
    print("old headers:", oh)
    print("new headers:", nh)
unit = next(h for h in nh if "unit" in h.lower())
role = next((h for h in nh if "role" in h.lower()), None)
print("responses: old", len(old), "new", len(new))

oid = {r["ID"] for r in old}
nid = {r["ID"] for r in new}
print("dropped IDs:", sorted(oid - nid))
added = [r for r in new if r["ID"] not in oid]
print("added responses:", len(added))
for r in added:
    print("  ", r["ID"], str(r["Completion time"])[:16], "|", r[unit],
          "| role:", r.get(role) if role else "")

cut = datetime.datetime(2026, 8, 29, 23, 59)
lm = [h for h in nh if "last modified" in h.lower()]
if lm:
    ed = [(r["ID"], r[unit]) for r in new if r["ID"] in oid
          and isinstance(r[lm[0]], datetime.datetime) and r[lm[0]] > cut]
    print("pre-existing responses modified after 08-29:", ed)
old_by = {r["ID"]: r for r in old}
changed = [(r["ID"], [k for k in nh if r.get(k) != old_by[r["ID"]].get(k)])
           for r in new if r["ID"] in oid and r != old_by[r["ID"]]]
print("pre-existing rows whose content differs (ID, columns):", changed)

# A response that is prose, not a list. Flagged, never parsed into products.
PROSE_MIN_WORDS = 12


def norm_key(s):
    """Lowercase and strip punctuation so alias lookup is forgiving."""
    s = s.lower().strip()
    s = re.sub(r"[^\w\s&/-]", " ", s)
    s = re.sub(r"[-_/]", " ", s)
    s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()
    return s


def strip_qty(item):
    """'MacBook x11' -> ('MacBook', 11). 'iPad x over 10' -> ('iPad', 10)."""
    m = re.search(r"\s+x\s*(?:at least\s*|over\s*)?(\d+)\s*$", item, re.I)
    if m:
        return item[: m.start()].strip(), int(m.group(1))
    return item.strip(), 1


.....
def strip_notes(item):
    """Drop respondent asides so the product name is left.

    'First Beat (not in use yet)' -> 'First Beat'
    'Track Man is about to be installed' -> 'Track Man'
    """
    item = re.sub(r"\s*\([^)]*\)\s*$", "", item).strip()
    item = re.split(r"\s+is about to be\b|\s+will be\b", item, flags=re.I)[0]
    return item.strip(" .,")


def resolve(raw_item, parent):
    """Map a raw string to (canonical, category, how_resolved)."""
    base, _qty = strip_qty(raw_item)
    base = strip_notes(base)
    k = norm_key(base)

    if k in NOISE:
        return "(excluded - not a technology)", "excluded", "noise"

    if k in ALIAS:
        c = ALIAS[k]
        return c, CATEGORY.get(c, "uncategorised"), "alias"

    # try 'Parent Item' e.g. parent='Catapult', item='Vault'
    if parent:
        pk = norm_key(f"{parent} {base}")

                  else "unit")

                    "source": source,
                })

# Tech_Inventory_Analysis

Cleaning and analysis of the Baylor Athletics Technology Inventory survey.

Companion to `~/DEV/SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework`, which holds the framework
documents, the form specs, and the form links. This folder holds only the
collected data and what comes out of it.

## Layout

```
raw/     frozen survey exports, date-stamped. never edited.
scripts/ clean_inventory.py (parser) + aliases.py (all judgement calls)
clean/   generated CSVs. delete and regenerate freely.
docs/    findings
deliverables/  anything that goes to Kenny / Jon Allen / ITS
```

## Run

```bash
cd ~/DEV/Tech_Inventory_Analysis
uv run --with openpyxl python3 scripts/clean_inventory.py
```

The script reads the newest `raw/Quick_Inventory_export_*.xlsx` and rewrites
everything in `clean/`. It is safe to run repeatedly.

Then rebuild the two documents. Both read `clean/*.csv`, so neither can drift
from the data, and both are set in the shared house style from
`~/DEV/Baylor_Doc_Style`:

```bash
uv run --with python-docx --with pypdfium2 python3 scripts/build_docx.py
uv run --with python-docx --with pypdfium2 python3 scripts/build_exec_summary.py
```

Each script writes the `.docx` and exports the `.pdf` from it through Word, so
the two files always match. `build_exec_summary.py` also **fails the build if
the summary spills past one page** — that is the whole point of the document,
so it is enforced rather than trusted.

**Open Microsoft Word before running it.** The script asks Word for the page
count and for the PDF, because Word is what the reader opens and its layout is
measurably taller than any stand-in. If Word is not already open it blocks on a
dialog the script cannot see, so the script falls back to an HTML twin, prints
a warning, and its page count should not be believed — an early version of this
document passed the twin at one page and was two pages in Word.

## Refresh with a newer export

1. Download the responses from Microsoft Forms.
2. Save as `raw/Quick_Inventory_export_YYYY-MM-DD.xlsx`.
3. Re-run the command above.
4. Check `clean/unmapped_review.csv`. If it has rows, add them to
   `scripts/aliases.py` and run again. It should end empty.

## Outputs

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `clean/tech_inventory_long.csv` | one row per unit × technology |
| `clean/tech_master.csv` | one row per distinct technology, with unit count |
| `clean/coverage.csv` | which of the 33 units responded, missed, or answered twice |
| `clean/stopped_using.csv` | technology retired in the last 12 months |
| `clean/unmapped_review.csv` | strings the alias map did not recognise |
| `clean/prose_responses_review.csv` | answers that were prose, not a list |
| `deliverables/Tech_Inventory_FINDINGS_ER_*.docx` / `.pdf` / `.html` | the full findings report — the working document |
| `deliverables/Tech_Inventory_EXEC_SUMMARY_ER_*.docx` / `.pdf` | the one-page summary — the document that gets forwarded |

Published copies of the deliverables live in OneDrive under
`00_Primary_Storage_Drive/05_SYSTEMS/SoftwareTechDocs/TechInventory_2026-08/`.
`raw/*.xlsx` is never copied there: it carries respondent names and emails.

## Ground rules

- **Nothing is guessed silently.** Unrecognised names go to
  `unmapped_review.csv` rather than being auto-matched.
- **All name merging lives in `scripts/aliases.py`.** The parser is mechanical.
- `raw/` is never modified. Re-analysis always starts from the frozen export.
- The export carries respondent names and email addresses. Strip those before
  anything is shared or published.

## House style

Both Word documents are set by `~/DEV/Baylor_Doc_Style`, measured from
`SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework/deliverables/Software_and_Technology_Management_Framework_DRAFT.docx`.
Change the module, never the individual builders — that is what keeps the
documents looking like one department wrote them.

## Two things Microsoft Forms does that will bite you

1. **The export declares a bogus sheet size** (`A1:A1`). openpyxl's fast
   `read_only` reader trusts it and returns an empty sheet. The script loads
   the workbook normally instead. Do not "optimise" that back.
2. **The system columns move between exports.** The 2026-08-29 export added a
   "Last modified time" column and shifted every question one place right.
   The script finds columns by header text, never by position.

## Status

Interim against the **2026-08-29** export: 37 responses, 27 of 33 units,
147 distinct technologies. Collection stays open to the department soft
deadline of 29 September 2026. See `docs/FINDINGS_2026-08-29.md`.

The 2026-08-24 export (15 responses) is kept in `raw/` for comparison. The
script always uses the newest file.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Tech_Inventory_Analysis

Cleaning and analysis of the Baylor Athletics Technology Inventory survey.

Companion to `~/DEV/SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework`, which holds the framework
documents, the form specs, and the form links. This folder holds only the
collected data and what comes out of it.

## Layout

```
raw/     frozen survey exports, date-stamped. never edited.
scripts/ clean_inventory.py (parser) + aliases.py (all judgement calls)
clean/   generated CSVs. delete and regenerate freely.
docs/    findings
deliverables/  anything that goes to Kenny / Jon Allen / ITS
```

## Run

```bash
cd ~/DEV/Tech_Inventory_Analysis
uv run --with openpyxl python3 scripts/clean_inventory.py
```

The script reads the newest `raw/Quick_Inventory_export_*.xlsx` and rewrites
everything in `clean/`. It is safe to run repeatedly.

Then rebuild the two documents. Both read `clean/*.csv`, so neither can drift
from the data, and both are set in the shared house style from
`~/DEV/Baylor_Doc_Style`:

```bash
uv run --with python-docx --with pypdfium2 python3 scripts/build_docx.py
uv run --with python-docx --with pypdfium2 python3 scripts/build_exec_summary.py
```

Each script writes the `.docx` and exports the `.pdf` from it through Word, so
the two files always match. `build_exec_summary.py` also **fails the build if
the summary spills past one page** — that is the whole point of the document,
so it is enforced rather than trusted.

**Open Microsoft Word before running it.** The script asks Word for the page
count and for the PDF, because Word is what the reader opens and its layout is
measurably taller than any stand-in. If Word is not already open it blocks on a
dialog the script cannot see, so the script falls back to an HTML twin, prints
a warning, and its page count should not be believed — an early version of this
document passed the twin at one page and was two pages in Word.

## Refresh with a newer export

1. Download the responses from Microsoft Forms.
2. Save as `raw/Quick_Inventory_export_YYYY-MM-DD.xlsx`.
3. Re-run the command above.
4. Check `clean/unmapped_review.csv`. If it has rows, add them to
   `scripts/aliases.py` and run again. It should end empty.

## Outputs

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `clean/tech_inventory_long.csv` | one row per unit × technology |
| `clean/tech_master.csv` | one row per distinct technology, with unit count |
| `clean/coverage.csv` | which of the 33 units responded, missed, or answered twice |
| `clean/stopped_using.csv` | technology retired in the last 12 months |
| `clean/unmapped_review.csv` | strings the alias map did not recognise |
| `clean/prose_responses_review.csv` | answers that were prose, not a list |
| `deliverables/Tech_Inventory_FINDINGS_ER_*.docx` / `.pdf` / `.html` | the full findings report — the working document |
| `deliverables/Tech_Inventory_EXEC_SUMMARY_ER_*.docx` / `.pdf` | the one-page summary — the document that gets forwarded |

Published copies of the deliverables live in OneDrive under
`00_Primary_Storage_Drive/05_SYSTEMS/SoftwareTechDocs/TechInventory_2026-08/`.
`raw/*.xlsx` is never copied there: it carries respondent names and emails.

## Ground rules

- **Nothing is guessed silently.** Unrecognised names go to
  `unmapped_review.csv` rather than being auto-matched.
- **All name merging lives in `scripts/aliases.py`.** The parser is mechanical.
- `raw/` is never modified. Re-analysis always starts from the frozen export.
- The export carries respondent names and email addresses. Strip those before
  anything is shared or published.

## House style

Both Word documents are set by `~/DEV/Baylor_Doc_Style`, measured from
`SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework/deliverables/Software_and_Technology_Management_Framework_DRAFT.docx`.
Change the module, never the individual builders — that is what keeps the
documents looking like one department wrote them.

## Two things Microsoft Forms does that will bite you

1. **The export declares a bogus sheet size** (`A1:A1`). openpyxl's fast
   `read_only` reader trusts it and returns an empty sheet. The script loads
   the workbook normally instead. Do not "optimise" that back.
2. **The system columns move between exports.** The 2026-08-29 export added a
   "Last modified time" column and shifted every question one place right.
   The script finds columns by header text, never by position.
3. **The OneDrive-synced workbook is not the Forms download.** Opening
   "Athletics Technology - Quick Inventory.xlsx" from OneDrive (2026-09-15)
   gives a file whose ID column is headed `Id`, which has no "Last modified
   time" column, and which **renumbers the rows** — the StatCrew retirement
   was response 5 in the 08-29 download and response 3 in the synced workbook.
   Match responses across exports on start and completion time, never on ID,
   and compare products on unit × product rather than diffing `clean/`.

## Status

Interim against the **2026-08-29** export: 37 responses, 27 of 33 units,
147 distinct technologies. Collection stays open to the department soft
deadline of 29 September 2026. See `docs/FINDINGS_2026-08-29.md`.

The 2026-08-24 export (15 responses) is kept in `raw/` for comparison. The
script always uses the newest file.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Baylor Athletics house style for Word documents.

One module, imported by every document builder, so the look is defined once.

    import sys
    sys.path.insert(0, "/Users/kristinarash/DEV/Baylor_Doc_Style")
    from baylor_docstyle import BaylorDoc

    d = BaylorDoc("Athletics Technology Inventory",
                  deck="What the department runs, and who runs it.",
                  status="Interim - collection open to 29 September 2026")
    d.meta([["Status", "Interim"], ["Prepared by", "Applied Performance"]])
    d.callout("How to read this", "Every figure is an interim read.")
    d.section("Coverage")
    d.para("Twenty-seven of thirty-two units have responded.")
    d.table(["Unit", "Responses"], [["Football", 3]])
    d.save("out.docx")

WHERE THE STYLE COMES FROM
--------------------------
Every measurement here was read out of
    SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework/deliverables/
        Software_and_Technology_Management_Framework_DRAFT.docx
which Eric chose on 2026-08-30 as the house look. Nothing is invented. If the
exemplar and this module ever disagree, the exemplar wins - re-measure it
rather than adjusting to taste.

TWO THINGS NOT TO "IMPROVE"
---------------------------
Calibri, everywhere. The exemplar sets no font on any run, so every size
inherits Normal. Calibri ships with Office, which is why the document survives
being emailed. Baylor's licensed faces live in ~/DEV/Baylor_Fonts, but a
document set in them renders as a fallback on any machine that lacks them.

No running header. The exemplar has an empty header and carries the document's
status in the meta block and the footer instead. That still puts the status on
every page, which is the constraint that matters.

INLINE BOLD
-----------
Every text argument accepts ``**like this**`` for inline bold.
"""

from docx import Document
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor

__all__ = ["BaylorDoc", "GREEN", "GOLD", "GREY", "CREAM", "INK", "BODY_FONT"]

# --- palette, straight from the exemplar ---------------------------------
GREEN = RGBColor(0x15, 0x47, 0x34)      # Baylor green: titles, headings, rules
GOLD = RGBColor(0xB8, 0x86, 0x0B)       # the eyebrow line only
GREY = RGBColor(0x59, 0x59, 0x59)       # decks, notes, the footer
CREAM = "FFF4DA"                        # callout fill
WHITE = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)      # text on a green table header
INK = None                              # body text: Word's default, not black

BODY_FONT = "Calibri"

# --- page and base paragraph ---------------------------------------------
MARGIN = dict(top=0.80, bottom=0.80, left=0.90, right=0.90)
BODY_SIZE = 10.5
BODY_AFTER = 6
LINE_SPACING = 1.0791666666666666       # the exemplar's exact value

EYEBROW_DEFAULT = "BAYLOR ATHLETICS  ·  APPLIED PERFORMANCE"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# low-level helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
.....
    are handed out automatically, so inserting a section never means renumbering
    the ones after it.
    """

    def __init__(self, title, deck=None, status=None,
                 eyebrow=EYEBROW_DEFAULT, footer_suffix="Baylor Athletics",
                 page_numbers=True):
        self.doc = Document()
        self.title = title
        self.status = status
        self._section_no = 0
        self._base_style()
        self._page_setup()
        self._footer(footer_suffix, page_numbers)
        self._title_block(title, deck, eyebrow)

    # -- setup -------------------------------------------------------------
    def _base_style(self):
        st = self.doc.styles["Normal"]
        st.font.name = BODY_FONT
        st.font.size = Pt(BODY_SIZE)
        st.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(BODY_AFTER)
        st.paragraph_format.line_spacing = LINE_SPACING

    def _page_setup(self):
        sec = self.doc.sections[0]
        sec.top_margin = Inches(MARGIN["top"])
        sec.bottom_margin = Inches(MARGIN["bottom"])
        sec.left_margin = Inches(MARGIN["left"])
        sec.right_margin = Inches(MARGIN["right"])
        self.text_width = 8.5 - MARGIN["left"] - MARGIN["right"]

    def _footer(self, suffix, page_numbers):
        """Centred, quiet, and carrying the document's status on every page."""
        fp = self.doc.sections[0].footer.paragraphs[0]
        fp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
        parts = [self.title]
        if self.status:
            parts.append(self.status)
        parts.append(suffix)
        r = fp.add_run("   ·   ".join(parts))
        r.font.name = BODY_FONT; r.font.size = Pt(7.5); r.font.color.rgb = GREY
        if page_numbers:
            r2 = fp.add_run("   ·   ")
            r2.font.name = BODY_FONT; r2.font.size = Pt(7.5)
            r2.font.color.rgb = GREY
            page_field(fp)

    def _title_block(self, title, deck, eyebrow):
        if eyebrow:
            p = self._p(space_after=1)
            add_runs(p, eyebrow, size=9, bold=True, color=GOLD)
        p = self._p(space_after=2)
        add_runs(p, title, size=19, bold=True, color=GREEN)
        if deck:
            p = self._p(space_after=10)
            add_runs(p, deck, size=11, italic=True, color=GREY)

    def _p(self, space_before=None, space_after=None, style=None):
        p = self.doc.add_paragraph(style=style) if style else self.doc.add_paragraph()
        if space_before is not None:
            p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(space_before)
        if space_after is not None:
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
        return p

    # -- content -----------------------------------------------------------
    def meta(self, rows, label_width=1.5):
        """The status block under the title. Borderless: it is a label/value
        list that happens to be laid out in a table, not a data table."""
        t = self.doc.add_table(rows=0, cols=2)
        t.style = "Normal Table"
        t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.LEFT
        for label, value in rows:
            cells = t.add_row().cells
            p = cells[0].paragraphs[0]
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
            add_runs(p, label, size=9, bold=True)
            p = cells[1].paragraphs[0]
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
            add_runs(p, value, size=9)
        for row in t.rows:
            row.cells[0].width = Inches(label_width)
            row.cells[1].width = Inches(self.text_width - label_width)
        self._p(space_after=4)
        return t

    def callout(self, head, body):
        """The cream box. For how to read the document, or a caveat that has to
        be seen before the reader starts."""
        t = self.doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=1)
        t.style = "Table Grid"
        cell = t.rows[0].cells[0]
        shade(cell, CREAM)
        p = cell.paragraphs[0]
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(1)
        add_runs(p, head, size=9.5, bold=True, color=GREEN)
        p = cell.add_paragraph()
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
        add_runs(p, body, size=9.5)
        cell.width = Inches(self.text_width)
        self._p(space_after=4)
        return t

    def section(self, text, numbered=True):
        """A top-level heading, numbered in sequence and underlined in green."""
        if numbered:
            self._section_no += 1
            text = "{}.  {}".format(self._section_no, text)
        p = self._p(space_before=14, space_after=5)
        # Never let a heading sit alone at the foot of a page. This is what
        # removes the need for hand-placed page breaks, which go stale as soon
        # as the content above them changes length.
        p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
        add_runs(p, text, size=13, bold=True, color=GREEN)
        bottom_rule(p)
        return p

    def subhead(self, text):
        p = self._p(space_before=10, space_after=3)
        p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
        add_runs(p, text, size=11.5, bold=True, color=GREEN)
        return p

    def para(self, text, space_before=None, space_after=BODY_AFTER):
        p = self._p(space_before=space_before, space_after=space_after)
        return add_runs(p, text)

    def note(self, text):
        """Small italic grey. A caveat that belongs beside the thing it
        qualifies rather than in a callout."""
        p = self._p(space_after=BODY_AFTER)
        return add_runs(p, text, size=9.5, italic=True, color=GREY)

    def small(self, text):
        """Small plain grey. A caption under a table."""
        p = self._p(space_after=BODY_AFTER)
        return add_runs(p, text, size=9.5, color=GREY)

    def bullets(self, items):
        for item in items:
            p = self.doc.add_paragraph(style="List Bullet")
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
            p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.4)
            p.paragraph_format.first_line_indent = Inches(-0.19)
            add_runs(p, item)

    def numbered(self, items):
        """A hanging numbered list. Used for recommended actions, where the
        number is referred to in conversation."""
        for i, item in enumerate(items, start=1):
            p = self._p(space_after=BODY_AFTER)
            p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.28)
            p.paragraph_format.first_line_indent = Inches(-0.28)
            r = p.add_run("{}.  ".format(i))
            r.font.name = BODY_FONT; r.font.size = Pt(BODY_SIZE)
            r.bold = True; r.font.color.rgb = GOLD
            add_runs(p, item)

    def quote(self, text):
        """A pulled quotation, indented and set in green italic."""
        p = self._p(space_after=BODY_AFTER)
        p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.3)
        return add_runs(p, "“{}”".format(text.strip("“”\"")),
                        size=11.5, italic=True, color=GREEN)

    def table(self, headers, rows, widths=None, numeric_cols=(),
              caption=None, compact=False):
        """A data table: green header band, white header text, thin grid."""
        t = self.doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers))
        t.style = "Table Grid"
        t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.LEFT
        pad = 0 if compact else 2
        for i, htext in enumerate(headers):
            cell = t.rows[0].cells[i]
            shade(cell, "154734")
            p = cell.paragraphs[0]
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(pad)
            if i in numeric_cols:
                p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT
            add_runs(p, htext, size=9.5, bold=True, color=WHITE)
        for row in rows:
            cells = t.add_row().cells
            for i, val in enumerate(row):
                p = cells[i].paragraphs[0]
                p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(pad)
                if i in numeric_cols:
                    p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT
                add_runs(p, val, size=9.5)
        if widths:
            for row in t.rows:
                for i, w in enumerate(widths):
                    row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)
        if not compact:
            self._p(space_after=2)
        if caption:
            self.small(caption)
        return t

    def page_break(self):
        self.doc.add_page_break()

    def spacer(self, points=4):
        self._p(space_after=points)

    # -- output ------------------------------------------------------------
    def save(self, path):
        self.doc.save(path)
        return path

.....

    """

    def __init__(self, title, deck=None, status=None,
                 eyebrow=EYEBROW_DEFAULT, footer_suffix="Baylor Athletics",
                 page_numbers=True):
        self.doc = Document()
        self.title = title
        self.status = status
        self._section_no = 0
        self._base_style()
        self._page_setup()
        self._footer(footer_suffix, page_numbers)
        self._title_block(title, deck, eyebrow)

    # -- setup -------------------------------------------------------------
    def _base_style(self):
        st = self.doc.styles["Normal"]
        st.font.name = BODY_FONT
        st.font.size = Pt(BODY_SIZE)
        st.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(BODY_AFTER)
        st.paragraph_format.line_spacing = LINE_SPACING

    def _page_setup(self):
        sec = self.doc.sections[0]
        sec.top_margin = Inches(MARGIN["top"])
        sec.bottom_margin = Inches(MARGIN["bottom"])
        sec.left_margin = Inches(MARGIN["left"])
        sec.right_margin = Inches(MARGIN["right"])
        self.text_width = 8.5 - MARGIN["left"] - MARGIN["right"]

    def _footer(self, suffix, page_numbers):
        """Centred, quiet, and carrying the document's status on every page."""
        fp = self.doc.sections[0].footer.paragraphs[0]
        fp.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
        parts = [self.title]
        if self.status:
            parts.append(self.status)
        parts.append(suffix)
        r = fp.add_run("   ·   ".join(parts))
        r.font.name = BODY_FONT; r.font.size = Pt(7.5); r.font.color.rgb = GREY
        if page_numbers:
            r2 = fp.add_run("   ·   ")
            r2.font.name = BODY_FONT; r2.font.size = Pt(7.5)
            r2.font.color.rgb = GREY
            page_field(fp)

    def _title_block(self, title, deck, eyebrow):
        if eyebrow:
            p = self._p(space_after=1)
            add_runs(p, eyebrow, size=9, bold=True, color=GOLD)
        p = self._p(space_after=2)
        add_runs(p, title, size=19, bold=True, color=GREEN)
        if deck:
            p = self._p(space_after=10)
            add_runs(p, deck, size=11, italic=True, color=GREY)

    def _p(self, space_before=None, space_after=None, style=None):
        p = self.doc.add_paragraph(style=style) if style else self.doc.add_paragraph()
        if space_before is not None:
            p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(space_before)
        if space_after is not None:
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)

        list that happens to be laid out in a table, not a data table."""
        t = self.doc.add_table(rows=0, cols=2)
        t.style = "Normal Table"
        t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.LEFT
        for label, value in rows:
            cells = t.add_row().cells

            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
            add_runs(p, label, size=9, bold=True)
            p = cells[1].paragraphs[0]
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
            add_runs(p, value, size=9)

        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)

        p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True

        return p

        p = self._p(space_after=BODY_AFTER)
        return add_runs(p, text, size=9.5, color=GREY)

    def bullets(self, items):

            p = self.doc.add_paragraph(style="List Bullet")
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(4)
            p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.4)
            p.paragraph_format.first_line_indent = Inches(-0.19)
