STATUS = "Interim — collection open to September 29, 2026"

# Headline figures from the previous run (2026-08-29 export), for comparison.
PREVIOUS = dict(date="August 29, 2026", submissions=37, units_self=27,
                products=147, athlete=60, single=110, retired=7)

PHANTOM_UNITS = {"Other"}   # a form option nobody selected; not a unit

PRETTY = {"video-analytics": "Video & analytics", "comms-media": "Comms & media",
          "office-general": "Office general", "equipment-ops": "Equipment ops",
          "athlete-management": "Athlete management", "ai-general": "AI tools",
          "food-travel": "Food & travel", "social-media": "Social media",
          "athlete-stipend": "Athlete stipend", "uncategorised": "Unidentified"}


def pretty(cat):
    return PRETTY.get(cat, cat.capitalize())


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# data
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def load():
    def rd(name):
        with open(os.path.join(CLEAN, name), encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return list(csv.DictReader(f))

    long_all = rd("tech_inventory_long.csv")
    master = [r for r in rd("tech_master.csv") if r["category"] != "excluded"]
    long = [r for r in long_all if r["category"] != "excluded"]
    return (master, long, long_all, rd("coverage.csv"), rd("stopped_using.csv"),
            rd("unmapped_review.csv"), rd("prose_responses_review.csv"))


def main():
    master, long, long_all, cov_all, stopped, unmapped, prose = load()
    by = {r["canonical"]: r for r in master}

    def units(name):
        return int(by[name]["unit_count"]) if name in by else 0

    cov = [r for r in cov_all if r["unit"] not in PHANTOM_UNITS]
    units_total = len(cov)
    units_self = [r for r in cov if r["status"] in ("responded", "MULTIPLE")]
    bo_only_units = [r["unit"] for r in cov if r["status"] == "BUSINESS OFFICE ONLY"]
    no_response = [r["unit"] for r in cov if r["status"] == "NO RESPONSE"]

    n_sub = len({r["response_id"] for r in long_all}
                | {r["response_id"] for r in stopped}
                | {r["response_id"] for r in prose})
    n_products = len(master)
    n_athlete = len([r for r in master if r["athlete_data_likely"] == "Y"])
    n_single = len([r for r in master if int(r["unit_count"]) == 1])
    n_mentions = len(long)
    n_excluded = len(long_all) - len(long)

    bo_rows = [r for r in long_all + stopped if r.get("source") == "business-office"]
    n_bo_entries = len({r["response_id"] for r in bo_rows})
    bo_units = sorted({r["unit"] for r in bo_rows})
    bo_only = [r for r in master if r.get("unit_count_self_reported") == "0"]

    in_use = {}
    for r in long:
        if r["status"] == "in_use":
            in_use.setdefault(r["canonical"], set()).add(r["unit"])
    planned = [r for r in long if r["status"] == "planned"
               and r["unit"] not in in_use.get(r["canonical"], set())]

    deck = ("{} submissions across the department, and a second view from the "
            "Business Office's records. Most of the technology here still sits "
            "with a single unit.".format(n_sub))
    d = BaylorDoc(TITLE, deck=deck, status=STATUS)

    d.meta([
        ["Status", "**Interim** — collection stays open to the department "
                   "soft deadline of September 29, 2026"],
        ["Date", long_date(EXPORT)],
        ["Source", "Microsoft Forms — Quick Inventory (5 questions), responses "
                   "workbook as of {}".format(long_date(EXPORT))],
        ["Previous run", "Export of {}".format(PREVIOUS["date"])],
        ["Prepared by", "Applied Performance, Baylor Athletics"],
        ["Companions", "Athletics Technology Inventory — Executive Summary "
                       "(one page); Technology Lists"],
    ])

    d.callout(
        "What changed since {}".format(PREVIOUS["date"]),
        "**{} new submissions**, and none of the earlier {} was changed or "
        "withdrawn. Tennis (M), Tennis (W) and Golf (M) responded for "
        "themselves. On September 14 the Business Office entered vendor lists "
        "from its purchasing and contract records for ten units, including "
        "Volleyball, whose own staff have not yet answered. Products named "
        "rose from {} to {}, and retirements from {} to {}."
        .format(n_sub - PREVIOUS["submissions"], PREVIOUS["submissions"],
                PREVIOUS["products"], n_products, PREVIOUS["retired"], len(stopped)))

    # --- 1 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("At a glance — where the inventory stands")
    d.table(
        ["Measure", "Now", PREVIOUS["date"].split(",")[0], "Note"],
        [["Submissions", n_sub, PREVIOUS["submissions"],
          "{} of them entered by the Business Office".format(n_bo_entries)],
         ["Units answering for themselves",
          "{} of {}".format(len(units_self), units_total),
          "{} of {}".format(PREVIOUS["units_self"], units_total),
          "Volleyball is covered only by the Business Office's list"
          if bo_only_units else "Interim"],
         ["Distinct products", n_products, PREVIOUS["products"],
          "Resolved from {} separate mentions".format(n_mentions)],
         ["Products touching athlete data", n_athlete, PREVIOUS["athlete"],
          "{}% of products, by category — a screening list".format(
              round(100 * n_athlete / n_products))],
         ["Products used by a single unit", n_single, PREVIOUS["single"],
          "{}% of products".format(round(100 * n_single / n_products))],
         ["Retired in the last 12 months", len(stopped), PREVIOUS["retired"],
          "Vendor data disposition not recorded"]],
        widths=[1.9, 0.75, 0.85, 3.2], numeric_cols=(1, 2))
    d.small("Units are counted out of {}: the form listed 33 options, and "
            "“Other” was never selected.".format(units_total))

    # --- 2 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Coverage — who has responded")
    d.para("**{} of {} units have answered for themselves.**".format(
        len(units_self), units_total)
        + (" {} {} covered only by the Business Office's vendor list, so the "
           "unit's own view of what it uses is still to come."
           .format(" and ".join(bo_only_units),
                   "is" if len(bo_only_units) == 1 else "are")
           if bo_only_units else "")
        + (" Still to respond: {}.".format(", ".join(no_response))
           if no_response else ""))

    d.subhead("Units that submitted more than once")
    multi = [(r["unit"], r["unit_responses"]) for r in cov if r["status"] == "MULTIPLE"]
    d.para(", ".join("{} ({})".format(u, n) for u, n in multi) + ".", space_after=4)
    d.para("These are different people describing different slices of the same "
           "unit. They are kept and tagged rather than merged. Business Office "
           "entries are counted separately and are not included here.")

    d.subhead("Coverage by unit")
    rows = []
    for r in cov:
        own, bo = int(r["unit_responses"]), int(r["business_office_entries"])
        label = {"responded": "Responded", "MULTIPLE": "{} people".format(own),
                 "BUSINESS OFFICE ONLY": "Business Office list only",
                 "NO RESPONSE": "Not yet in"}.get(r["status"], r["status"])
        rows.append([r["unit"], own, bo or "", label])
    d.table(["Unit", "Unit responses", "Business Office", "Status"], rows,
            widths=[2.9, 1.1, 1.1, 1.6], numeric_cols=(1, 2))

    # --- 3 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("A second source — the Business Office's records")
    d.para("The Business Office submitted **{} entries covering {} units**: two "
           "in August (Baseball and Football) and ten on September 14. They are "
           "short vendor lists drawn from purchasing and contract records rather "
           "than descriptions of day-to-day use, and the Business Office's own "
           "entry is a department-wide contract list."
           .format(n_bo_entries, len(bo_units)))
    d.para("That makes them the cross-check the previous report recommended. "
           "Every row in the data now records whether a unit named a product "
           "itself or it came from the Business Office, so the two views can be "
           "read side by side. Where they differ, neither is wrong: a contract "
           "shows what is paid for, and a unit's answer shows what is used.")
    d.para("Products named by more than one unit through the Business Office "
           "include Hudl ({} units, {} by the unit itself) and DVSport ({} units, "
           "{} by the unit itself)."
           .format(units("Hudl"), by["Hudl"]["unit_count_self_reported"],
                   units("DVSport"), by["DVSport"]["unit_count_self_reported"]))

    d.subhead("Products known only from the Business Office's lists")
    d.table(["Product", "Category", "Listed for"],
            [[r["canonical"], pretty(r["category"]), r["units"]]
             for r in sorted(bo_only, key=lambda r: (r["category"], r["canonical"]))],
            widths=[2.2, 1.6, 2.9])
    if "Recovery Record" in by:
        d.para("**Recovery Record** appears only here. It is an eating-disorder "
               "treatment app, so it holds athlete health information, and no "
               "unit named it. It belongs at the front of the detailed second "
               "pass.", space_before=3)

    # --- 4 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("The estate — most of it sits with one unit")
    d.para("{} of {} products were named by a single unit. That long tail — not "
           "the vendor overlap — is the finding. It is the population no "
           "central process currently sees.".format(n_single, n_products))
    d.para("It includes AI tools adopted locally (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, "
           "Microsoft Copilot, Grammarly), a scatter of productivity and "
           "communication apps (Notion, Asana, Todoist, Padlet, Sling, GroupMe, "
           "Jotform), and one-off athlete-facing systems (Nix Biosensors, Calera "
           "CORE, Boost Treadmills, C3 Logix, Hologic DXA, Foresight GCQuad, "
           "Edgertronic).")

    d.subhead("Distinct products by category")
    cats = {}
    for r in master:
        cats[r["category"]] = cats.get(r["category"], 0) + 1
    d.table(["Category", "Products"],
            [[pretty(k), v] for k, v in sorted(cats.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])],
            widths=[3.0, 1.0], numeric_cols=(1,))

    d.subhead("Products used by three or more units")
    d.table(["Product", "Units", "Named by the unit", "Category"],
            [[r["canonical"], int(r["unit_count"]),
              int(r["unit_count_self_reported"]), pretty(r["category"])]
             for r in master if int(r["unit_count"]) >= 3],
            widths=[2.3, 0.7, 1.4, 2.3], numeric_cols=(1, 2))
    top = max(master, key=lambda r: int(r["unit_count"]))
    d.para("**{}, at {} units, is the only thing close to a department-wide "
           "system.** Everything below it is departmental at best."
           .format(top["canonical"], top["unit_count"]), space_before=3)

    # --- 5 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Overlap — several vendors, one job")
    d.para("The consolidation conversation is answerable with counts rather than "
           "estimates. One new overlap arrived with this export: **Hawkin "
           "Dynamics**, a force plate system, listed for Volleyball alongside "
           "VALD in other units.")
    n_video = len([r for r in master if r["category"] == "video-analytics"])
    d.table(["Job", "Vendors in use (units)"],
            [["Athlete tracking",
              "Catapult ({}), Kinexon ({}), Polar ({}); Firstbeat arriving".format(
                  units("Catapult"), units("Kinexon"), len(in_use.get("Polar", ())))],
             ["Force & speed testing",
              "VALD ({}), Perch ({}), GymAware ({}), Hawkin Dynamics ({}), TMG ({})"
              .format(units("VALD"), units("Perch"), units("GymAware"),
                      units("Hawkin Dynamics"), units("TMG"))],
             ["Athlete management",
              "Teamworks ({}), Kitman Labs ({}), XPS Network ({})".format(
                  units("Teamworks"), units("Kitman Labs"), units("XPS Network"))],
             ["Video & analytics",
              "{} products, led by Hudl ({}), DVSport ({}) and Synergy Sports ({})"
              .format(n_video, units("Hudl"), units("DVSport"),
                      units("Synergy Sports"))]],
            widths=[1.9, 4.8])

    # --- 6 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Open items — {} products retired, no recorded disposition"
              .format(len(stopped)))
    d.para("Every retirement in the last twelve months may have left data with a "
           "vendor. The short form did not ask where, so the answer is not "
           "captured anywhere yet. Confirming what each vendor retained is the "
           "most concrete, closeable action in this dataset.")
    d.table(["Unit", "Product", "Vendor retention"],
            [[r["unit"], r["canonical"], "Not asked"]
             for r in sorted(stopped, key=lambda r: (r["canonical"], r["unit"]))],
            widths=[2.3, 2.3, 2.1])

    retired_elsewhere = {}
    for r in stopped:
        others = in_use.get(r["canonical"], set()) - {r["unit"]}
        if others:
            retired_elsewhere.setdefault(r["canonical"], [set(), others])[0].add(r["unit"])
    for product, (gone, still) in sorted(retired_elsewhere.items()):
        d.subhead("{} is retired by {} and still in use by {}".format(
            product, " and ".join(sorted(gone)), " and ".join(sorted(still))))
        d.para("Surfacing that automatically, and confirming what a vendor "
               "retains when a unit stops using a product, are two capabilities "
               "the framework would add.")

    if planned:
        d.subhead("Coming online")
        d.bullets(["**{}** — {}, not yet in use.".format(r["unit"], r["canonical"])
                   for r in planned])
        d.para("None can be confirmed against a documented vetting step, because "
               "the short form did not ask.")

    # --- 7 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Signal — one unit answered the underlying question unprompted")
    d.quote("Everything we have has gone through ITS approval, so they have "
            "the list already.")
    d.para("Broadcast and Big Screens, who then listed thirteen vendors: "
           "Ross Video, Evertz, Grass Valley, Calrec, Adder, EditShare, "
           "Riedel, Daktronics, ANC, Haivision, Vyvx, LTN and Switch.")
    d.para("That list is worth checking against the ITS IDEA form history. If "
           "it matches, it is a working baseline for what full compliance "
           "looks like in practice.")

    # --- 8 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Limits — what this data cannot answer")
    d.para("The short form asked five questions. Four things the framework "
           "needs were not among them.")
    d.bullets([
        "**Does it involve student-athlete information, and what kind?** The "
        "{}-product figure is a category inference, not a respondent answer. "
        "Treat it as a screening list.".format(n_athlete),
        "**How is it paid for, and when does the contract end?** The Business "
        "Office's lists show what is under contract for {} units, but not terms "
        "or end dates.".format(len(bo_units)),
        "**Did it go through the ITS IDEA form?** Not asked, so the bypass "
        "rate remains an estimate rather than a measured number.",
        "**Does a vendor still hold data from a discontinued product?** Not "
        "asked. {} retirements, no dispositions recorded.".format(len(stopped)),
    ])
    d.para("The seventeen-question detailed form was written to close exactly "
           "these four gaps. It has not run yet.")

    # --- 9 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Next — recommended steps")
    steps = []
    if bo_only_units or no_response:
        steps.append("**Ask {} for {} own list before September 29.** The "
                     "Business Office's entry shows what is paid for; the unit's "
                     "answer shows what is used.".format(
                         " and ".join(bo_only_units + no_response),
                         "its" if len(bo_only_units + no_response) == 1 else "their"))
    steps += [
        "**Close the retirement loop.** {} products retired, and what each vendor "
        "retained is not recorded. Small, concrete, demonstrable.".format(len(stopped)),
        "**Run the detailed form as a targeted second pass.** Aimed at the {} "
        "athlete-data candidates, starting with the ones only the Business Office "
        "named, rather than at all {} products.".format(n_athlete, n_products),
        "**Compare against the ITS IDEA form history.** The Business Office's "
        "lists are one independent source; the IDEA history is the other, and "
        "together they produce the bypass number without a survey question.",
        "**Decide on the long tail.** {} single-unit products is a policy "
        "question rather than a data question, and it is the one this exercise "
        "exists to raise.".format(n_single),
    ]
    d.numbered(steps)

    # --- 10 ----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Method — how to read these numbers")
    d.para("Free-text answers were parsed mechanically. Every decision about "
           "whether two strings name the same product is written down and "
           "reversible, and unrecognised names are held for review rather than "
           "assigned to a guess. Responses are matched across exports on their "
           "start and completion times, because the responses workbook renumbers "
           "them.")

    d.subhead("Judgement calls worth confirming")
    d.bullets([
        "**Business Office entries** — every response with the role “Business "
        "Office” is tagged as that source, including its own department-wide "
        "list. Unit counts include them; the “named by the unit” column does "
        "not.",
        "**Hudl** — “HUDL Statsbomb”, “HUDL WyScout” and “HUDL Focus” merged. "
        "Same vendor, three products. This is why Soccer appears as both using "
        "and having stopped Hudl.",
        "**Whistle** — one unit wrote “Whistle (DataViz)”, others wrote bare "
        "“DataViz”. Assumed to be the same product. Softball's “Whistlestop” is "
        "not assumed to be Whistle.",
        "**Teamworks** — “TW Nutrition”, “Teamworks Hub” and “Teamworks "
        "Intelligence” folded in as modules, and “Notemeal”, which Teamworks "
        "acquired and now sells as Teamworks Nutrition.",
        "**Google suite** — Google Docs, Sheets, Forms and Calendar fold into "
        "Google Drive, the way Word, Excel and Outlook fold into Microsoft Office.",
        "**INFLCR** — Tennis wrote “Influencer”, read as INFLCR.",
        "**6-4-3 Charts** — “643 Charts”, “6-4-3” and “643 analytics” merged.",
        "**Red Card** — the student-athlete meal-money stipend. It carries "
        "athlete identity and transaction records, so it is counted as athlete "
        "data despite not being a performance system.",
        "**Excluded** — {} fragments that are not technology: section headers "
        "respondents typed, and physical equipment such as helmets, jerseys and "
        "racquet brands.".format(n_excluded),
    ])

    d.subhead("Names still to be identified")
    if unmapped:
        seen, rows = set(), []
        for r in unmapped:
            if (r["raw_item"], r["unit"]) not in seen:
                seen.add((r["raw_item"], r["unit"]))
                rows.append([r["raw_item"], r["unit"]])
        d.table(["Named", "By"], rows, widths=[2.4, 2.6])
        d.para("Out of {} raw mentions, these are the only names that could "
               "not be resolved to a known product."
               .format(len(long_all)), space_before=2)
    else:
        d.para("None outstanding.")

    d.small("Every figure in this document regenerates from the raw export. "
            "Respondent names and email addresses remain in the source file "
            "and appear nowhere in this report.")

    os.makedirs(DELIV, exist_ok=True)
    docx_path = d.save(os.path.join(DELIV, STEM + ".docx"))
    print("wrote", docx_path)
    print("units {}/{} self-reported · products {} · athlete-data {} · single-unit {} "
          "· Business Office entries {} · BO-only products {}".format(
              len(units_self), units_total, n_products, n_athlete, n_single,
              n_bo_entries, len(bo_only)))

    pdf_path = os.path.join(DELIV, STEM + ".pdf")
    n = word_pdf(docx_path, pdf_path)
    if n is None:
        print("[warn] Word did not answer, so no PDF was exported and the .pdf "
              "beside this file is stale. Open Microsoft Word and re-run.")
    else:
        print("wrote", pdf_path, "(from Word) ->", n, "page(s)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build the Technology Lists companion: every product in use, and every product
discontinued in the last 12 months.

Run:
    uv run --with python-docx --with pypdfium2 python scripts/build_tech_lists.py

The 2026-09-01 version of this document was built outside this repo and then
edited by hand. This builder reproduces the edited version's shape - title,
one alphabetical line per product, the discontinued list - so it regenerates
from clean/*.csv instead of being retyped for every export.

Two markers the 09-01 version did not need:
  - a dagger for products known only from the Business Office's purchasing and
    contract lists, which no unit named itself (from the 09-15 export on);
  - "coming online" for products every mention of which says not yet in use.
"""

import csv
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from doc_platform import (add_doc_style_to_path, export_date,  # noqa: E402
                          long_date, word_pdf)
add_doc_style_to_path()
from baylor_docstyle import BaylorDoc, GREY, add_runs  # noqa: E402

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
CLEAN = os.path.join(ROOT, "clean")
DELIV = os.path.join(ROOT, "deliverables")
EXPORT = export_date()
STEM = "Tech_Inventory_TECH_LISTS_ER_{}".format(EXPORT.isoformat())

TITLE = "Baylor Athletics Technology Inventory"
STATUS = "Interim — collection open to September 29, 2026"

PRETTY = {
    "video-analytics": "Video and analytics", "comms-media": "Communications and media",
    "performance": "Performance", "admin": "Administration", "broadcast": "Broadcast",
    "productivity": "Productivity", "medical": "Medical",
    "office-general": "Office and general", "recruiting": "Recruiting",
    "hardware": "Hardware", "equipment-ops": "Equipment operations",
    "academic": "Academic", "athlete-management": "Athlete management",
    "ai-general": "AI tools", "facility": "Facility", "ticketing": "Ticketing",
    "food-travel": "Food and travel", "athlete-stipend": "Athlete stipend",
    "social-media": "Social media", "uncategorised": "Unidentified (being confirmed)",
}


def rd(name):
    with open(os.path.join(CLEAN, name), encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return list(csv.DictReader(f))


def main():
    master = [r for r in rd("tech_master.csv") if r["category"] != "excluded"]
    long = [r for r in rd("tech_inventory_long.csv") if r["category"] != "excluded"]
    stopped = rd("stopped_using.csv")

    statuses = {}
    for r in long:
        statuses.setdefault(r["canonical"], set()).add(r["status"])
    coming = {c for c, s in statuses.items() if s == {"planned"}}
    in_use_units = {}
    for r in long:
        if r["status"] == "in_use":
            in_use_units.setdefault(r["canonical"], set()).add(r["unit"])

    d = BaylorDoc(TITLE, deck="Technology Lists  ·  as of {}".format(long_date(EXPORT)),
                  status=STATUS, eyebrow=None)

    # --- 1 ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Technology currently in use  ({} products)".format(len(master)))
    d.note("Alphabetical. Bold marks products named by three or more units; the "
           "unit count follows products named by more than one. † marks products "
           "known only from the Business Office's purchasing and contract lists, "
           "which no unit named itself.")
    for r in sorted(master, key=lambda r: r["canonical"].lower()):
        n = int(r["unit_count"])
        p = d._p(space_after=0)
        add_runs(p, "**{}**".format(r["canonical"]) if n >= 3 else r["canonical"], size=9.5)
        if n > 1:
            add_runs(p, "  ({} units)".format(n), size=9.5)
        if r.get("unit_count_self_reported") == "0":
            add_runs(p, " †", size=9.5)
        if r["canonical"] in coming:
            add_runs(p, "  coming online", size=9.5, italic=True, color=GREY)
        add_runs(p, "  " + PRETTY.get(r["category"], r["category"]),
                 size=9.5, italic=True, color=GREY)

    # --- 2 ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Technology discontinued in the last 12 months  ({})".format(len(stopped)))
    still = []
    for r in stopped:
        others = in_use_units.get(r["canonical"], set()) - {r["unit"]}
        if others:
            still.append("{} is retired by {} and still listed as in use by {}"
                         .format(r["canonical"], r["unit"], ", ".join(sorted(others))))
    d.note("As reported by each unit. Whether the vendor still holds data from any "
           "of these was not asked on the short form and is not recorded."
           + ("" if not still else " " + "; ".join(still) + "."))
    for r in sorted(stopped, key=lambda r: (r["canonical"].lower(), r["unit"])):
        p = d._p(space_after=0)
        add_runs(p, r["canonical"], size=9.5)
        add_runs(p, "  " + r["unit"], size=9.5, italic=True, color=GREY)

    os.makedirs(DELIV, exist_ok=True)
    docx_path = d.save(os.path.join(DELIV, STEM + ".docx"))
    print("wrote", docx_path)
    print("in use {} · coming online {} · Business Office only {} · discontinued {}".format(
        len(master), len(coming),
        sum(r.get("unit_count_self_reported") == "0" for r in master), len(stopped)))

    pdf_path = os.path.join(DELIV, STEM + ".pdf")
    n = word_pdf(docx_path, pdf_path)
    if n is None:
        print("[warn] Word did not answer, so no PDF was exported.")
    else:
        print("wrote", pdf_path, "(from Word) ->", n, "page(s)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Baylor Athletics Technology Inventory
Executive Summary
1.  In brief
Every unit was asked to complete a five-question survey naming the technology it uses. 31 of 32 units have answered, describing 185 products. The Business Office also entered vendor lists from its purchasing and contract records for 12 units, including Volleyball, whose own staff have not yet answered. Collection stays open to September 29. The full list of products in use and products retired in the last 12 months is a separate document.

7.  Signal — one unit answered the underlying question unprompted
“Everything we have has gone through ITS approval, so they have the list already.”
Broadcast and Big Screens, who then listed thirteen vendors: Ross Video, Evertz, Grass Valley, Calrec, Adder, EditShare, Riedel, Daktronics, ANC, Haivision, Vyvx, LTN and Switch.
That list is worth checking against the ITS IDEA form history. If it matches, it is a working baseline for what full compliance looks like in practice.
8.  Limits — what this data cannot answer
The short form asked five questions. Four things the framework needs were not among them.
Does it involve student-athlete information, and what kind? The 75-product figure is a category inference, not a respondent answer. Treat it as a screening list.
How is it paid for, and when does the contract end? The Business Office's lists show what is under contract for 12 units, but not terms or end dates.
Did it go through the ITS IDEA form? Not asked, so the bypass rate remains an estimate rather than a measured number.
Does a vendor still hold data from a discontinued product? Not asked. 9 retirements, no dispositions recorded.
The seventeen-question detailed form was written to close exactly these four gaps. It has not run yet.
9.  Next — recommended steps
1.  Ask Volleyball for its own list before September 29. The Business Office's entry shows what is paid for; the unit's answer shows what is used.
2.  Close the retirement loop. 9 products retired, and what each vendor retained is not recorded. Small, concrete, demonstrable.
3.  Run the detailed form as a targeted second pass. Aimed at the 75 athlete-data candidates, starting with the ones only the Business Office named, rather than at all 185 products.
4.  Compare against the ITS IDEA form history. The Business Office's lists are one independent source; the IDEA history is the other, and together they produce the bypass number without a survey question.
5.  Decide on the long tail. 120 single-unit products is a policy question rather than a data question, and it is the one this exercise exists to raise.
10.  Method — how to read these numbers
Free-text answers were parsed mechanically. Every decision about whether two strings name the same product is written down and reversible, and unrecognised names are held for review rather than assigned to a guess. Responses are matched across exports on their start and completion times, because the responses workbook renumbers them.

Business Office entries — every response with the role “Business Office” is tagged as that source, including its own department-wide list. Unit counts include them; the “named by the unit” column does not.
Hudl — “HUDL Statsbomb”, “HUDL WyScout” and “HUDL Focus” merged. Same vendor, three products. This is why Soccer appears as both using and having stopped Hudl.
Whistle — one unit wrote “Whistle (DataViz)”, others wrote bare “DataViz”. Assumed to be the same product. Softball's “Whistlestop” is not assumed to be Whistle.
Teamworks — “TW Nutrition”, “Teamworks Hub” and “Teamworks Intelligence” folded in as modules, and “Notemeal”, which Teamworks acquired and now sells as Teamworks Nutrition.
Google suite — Google Docs, Sheets, Forms and Calendar fold into Google Drive, the way Word, Excel and Outlook fold into Microsoft Office.
INFLCR — Tennis wrote “Influencer”, read as INFLCR.
6-4-3 Charts — “643 Charts”, “6-4-3” and “643 analytics” merged.
Red Card — the student-athlete meal-money stipend. It carries athlete identity and transaction records, so it is counted as athlete data despite not being a performance system.
Excluded — 21 fragments that are not technology: section headers respondents typed, and physical equipment such as helmets, jerseys and racquet brands.

Out of 467 raw mentions, these are the only names that could not be resolved to a known product.
Every figure in this document regenerates from the raw export. Respondent names and email addresses remain in the source file and appear nowhere in this report.

# Tech_Inventory_Analysis

Cleaning and analysis of the Baylor Athletics Technology Inventory survey.

Companion to `~/DEV/SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework`, which holds the framework
documents, the form specs, and the form links. This folder holds only the
collected data and what comes out of it.

## Layout

```
raw/     frozen survey exports, date-stamped. never edited.
scripts/ clean_inventory.py (parser) + aliases.py (all judgement calls)
clean/   generated CSVs. delete and regenerate freely.
docs/    findings
deliverables/  anything that goes to Kenny / Jon Allen / ITS
```

## Run

```bash
cd ~/DEV/Tech_Inventory_Analysis
uv run --with openpyxl python3 scripts/clean_inventory.py
```

The script reads the newest `raw/Quick_Inventory_export_*.xlsx` and rewrites
everything in `clean/`. It is safe to run repeatedly.

Then rebuild the two documents. Both read `clean/*.csv`, so neither can drift
from the data, and both are set in the shared house style from
`~/DEV/Baylor_Doc_Style`:

```bash
uv run --with python-docx --with pypdfium2 python3 scripts/build_docx.py
uv run --with python-docx --with pypdfium2 python3 scripts/build_exec_summary.py
```

Each script writes the `.docx` and exports the `.pdf` from it through Word, so
the two files always match. `build_exec_summary.py` also **fails the build if
the summary spills past one page** — that is the whole point of the document,
so it is enforced rather than trusted.

**Open Microsoft Word before running it.** The script asks Word for the page
count and for the PDF, because Word is what the reader opens and its layout is
measurably taller than any stand-in. If Word is not already open it blocks on a
dialog the script cannot see, so the script falls back to an HTML twin, prints
a warning, and its page count should not be believed — an early version of this
document passed the twin at one page and was two pages in Word.

## Refresh with a newer export

1. Download the responses from Microsoft Forms.
2. Save as `raw/Quick_Inventory_export_YYYY-MM-DD.xlsx`.
3. Re-run the command above.
4. Check `clean/unmapped_review.csv`. If it has rows, add them to
   `scripts/aliases.py` and run again. It should end empty.

## Outputs

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `clean/tech_inventory_long.csv` | one row per unit × technology |
| `clean/tech_master.csv` | one row per distinct technology, with unit count |
| `clean/coverage.csv` | which of the 33 units responded, missed, or answered twice |
| `clean/stopped_using.csv` | technology retired in the last 12 months |
| `clean/unmapped_review.csv` | strings the alias map did not recognise |
| `clean/prose_responses_review.csv` | answers that were prose, not a list |
| `deliverables/Tech_Inventory_FINDINGS_ER_*.docx` / `.pdf` / `.html` | the full findings report — the working document |
| `deliverables/Tech_Inventory_EXEC_SUMMARY_ER_*.docx` / `.pdf` | the one-page summary — the document that gets forwarded |

Published copies of the deliverables live in OneDrive under
`00_Primary_Storage_Drive/05_SYSTEMS/SoftwareTechDocs/TechInventory_2026-08/`.
`raw/*.xlsx` is never copied there: it carries respondent names and emails.

## Ground rules

- **Nothing is guessed silently.** Unrecognised names go to
  `unmapped_review.csv` rather than being auto-matched.
- **All name merging lives in `scripts/aliases.py`.** The parser is mechanical.
- `raw/` is never modified. Re-analysis always starts from the frozen export.
- The export carries respondent names and email addresses. Strip those before
  anything is shared or published.

## House style

Both Word documents are set by `~/DEV/Baylor_Doc_Style`, measured from
`SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework/deliverables/Software_and_Technology_Management_Framework_DRAFT.docx`.
Change the module, never the individual builders — that is what keeps the
documents looking like one department wrote them.

## Three things Microsoft Forms does that will bite you

1. **The export declares a bogus sheet size** (`A1:A1`). openpyxl's fast
   `read_only` reader trusts it and returns an empty sheet. The script loads
   the workbook normally instead. Do not "optimise" that back.
2. **The system columns move between exports.** The 2026-08-29 export added a
   "Last modified time" column and shifted every question one place right.
   The script finds columns by header text, never by position.
3. **The OneDrive-synced workbook is not the Forms download.** Opening
   "Athletics Technology - Quick Inventory.xlsx" from OneDrive (2026-09-15)
   gives a file whose ID column is headed `Id`, which has no "Last modified
   time" column, and which **renumbers the rows** — the StatCrew retirement
   was response 5 in the 08-29 download and response 3 in the synced workbook.
   Match responses across exports on start and completion time, never on ID,
   and compare products on unit × product rather than diffing `clean/`.

## Status

Interim against the **2026-08-29** export: 37 responses, 27 of 33 units,
147 distinct technologies. Collection stays open to the department soft
deadline of 29 September 2026. See `docs/FINDINGS_2026-08-29.md`.

The 2026-08-24 export (15 responses) is kept in `raw/` for comparison. The
script always uses the newest file.

# Tech_Inventory_Analysis

Cleaning and analysis of the Baylor Athletics Technology Inventory survey.

Companion to `~/DEV/SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework`, which holds the framework
documents, the form specs, and the form links. This folder holds only the
collected data and what comes out of it.

## Layout

```
raw/     frozen survey exports, date-stamped. never edited.
scripts/ clean_inventory.py (parser) + aliases.py (all judgement calls)
clean/   generated CSVs. delete and regenerate freely.
docs/    findings
deliverables/  anything that goes to Kenny / Jon Allen / ITS
```

## Run

```bash
cd ~/DEV/Tech_Inventory_Analysis
uv run --with openpyxl python3 scripts/clean_inventory.py
```

The script reads the newest `raw/Quick_Inventory_export_*.xlsx` and rewrites
everything in `clean/`. It is safe to run repeatedly.

Then rebuild the two documents. Both read `clean/*.csv`, so neither can drift
from the data, and both are set in the shared house style from
`~/DEV/Baylor_Doc_Style`:

```bash
uv run --with python-docx --with pypdfium2 python3 scripts/build_docx.py
uv run --with python-docx --with pypdfium2 python3 scripts/build_exec_summary.py
```

Each script writes the `.docx` and exports the `.pdf` from it through Word, so
the two files always match. `build_exec_summary.py` also **fails the build if
the summary spills past one page** — that is the whole point of the document,
so it is enforced rather than trusted.

**Open Microsoft Word before running it.** The script asks Word for the page
count and for the PDF, because Word is what the reader opens and its layout is
measurably taller than any stand-in. If Word is not already open it blocks on a
dialog the script cannot see, so the script falls back to an HTML twin, prints
a warning, and its page count should not be believed — an early version of this
document passed the twin at one page and was two pages in Word.

## Refresh with a newer export

1. Download the responses from Microsoft Forms.
2. Save as `raw/Quick_Inventory_export_YYYY-MM-DD.xlsx`.
3. Re-run the command above.
4. Check `clean/unmapped_review.csv`. If it has rows, add them to
   `scripts/aliases.py` and run again. It should end empty.

## Outputs

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `clean/tech_inventory_long.csv` | one row per unit × technology |
| `clean/tech_master.csv` | one row per distinct technology, with unit count |
| `clean/coverage.csv` | which of the 33 units responded, missed, or answered twice |
| `clean/stopped_using.csv` | technology retired in the last 12 months |
| `clean/unmapped_review.csv` | strings the alias map did not recognise |
| `clean/prose_responses_review.csv` | answers that were prose, not a list |
| `deliverables/Tech_Inventory_FINDINGS_ER_*.docx` / `.pdf` / `.html` | the full findings report — the working document |
| `deliverables/Tech_Inventory_EXEC_SUMMARY_ER_*.docx` / `.pdf` | the one-page summary — the document that gets forwarded |

Published copies of the deliverables live in OneDrive under
`00_Primary_Storage_Drive/05_SYSTEMS/SoftwareTechDocs/TechInventory_2026-08/`.
`raw/*.xlsx` is never copied there: it carries respondent names and emails.

## Ground rules

- **Nothing is guessed silently.** Unrecognised names go to
  `unmapped_review.csv` rather than being auto-matched.
- **All name merging lives in `scripts/aliases.py`.** The parser is mechanical.
- `raw/` is never modified. Re-analysis always starts from the frozen export.
- The export carries respondent names and email addresses. Strip those before
  anything is shared or published.

## House style

Both Word documents are set by `~/DEV/Baylor_Doc_Style`, measured from
`SoftwareTech_Mgmt_Framework/deliverables/Software_and_Technology_Management_Framework_DRAFT.docx`.
Change the module, never the individual builders — that is what keeps the
documents looking like one department wrote them.

## Three things Microsoft Forms does that will bite you

1. **The export declares a bogus sheet size** (`A1:A1`). openpyxl's fast
   `read_only` reader trusts it and returns an empty sheet. The script loads
   the workbook normally instead. Do not "optimise" that back.
2. **The system columns move between exports.** The 2026-08-29 export added a
   "Last modified time" column and shifted every question one place right.
   The script finds columns by header text, never by position.
3. **The OneDrive-synced workbook is not the Forms download.** Opening
   "Athletics Technology - Quick Inventory.xlsx" from OneDrive (2026-09-15)
   gives a file whose ID column is headed `Id`, which has no "Last modified
   time" column, and which **renumbers the rows** — the StatCrew retirement
   was response 5 in the 08-29 download and response 3 in the synced workbook.
   Match responses across exports on start and completion time, never on ID,
   and compare products on unit × product rather than diffing `clean/`.

## Status

Interim against the **2026-09-15** export: 51 responses, 31 of 32 units
answering for themselves (Volleyball covered only by a Business Office entry),
185 distinct products. Collection stays open to the department soft deadline of
29 September 2026. See `docs/FINDINGS_2026-09-15.md`.

The 2026-08-24 (15 responses) and 2026-08-29 (37 responses) exports are kept in
`raw/` for comparison. The script always uses the newest file.

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\eric_rash\.claude\skills\memory-write

# Memory Write

## Outcome
- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."

## Pick the tier first

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"

**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)

**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`

## Steps

1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
2. **Read** the target file in full.
3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
5. **Write** the change.
   - Tier A: create a new file with proper frontmatter (name, description, metadata.type) and add a one-line pointer to that slug's `MEMORY.md` index. `name:` follows the rule below.
   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.
6. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

## The `name:` field — bare kebab slug

**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
it in `name:` is the third copy.

| File | `name:` |
|---|---|
| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |
| `reference_baylor-house-style.md` | `baylor-house-style` |
| `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` | `project-idea-capture` |

Note the last row: strip only the **leading** token. `feedback_project_idea_capture.md`
is a feedback memory *about* project-idea capture — its name keeps the word `project`.

`[[links]]` target this bare name, never the filename and never a prefixed variant.

This rule exists because it was previously unwritten: an audit on 2026-09-02 found the
corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in
isolation, so without a stated rule the split regrows on every write.

## Actions

- **add** — append (default)
- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder

When the user asks about past context, decisions, or "did we already…?", climb in order and stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run memsearch when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword across all indexed paths: Tier A files (including the Windows-machine slugs), daily logs, transcripts.
3. **L2** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
4. **L3** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
5. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

## Daily compiled logs — read-only

`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` is produced by `claude-memory-compiler` through its own SessionEnd/PreCompact hooks, and injected by its own SessionStart hook.

- **Never hand-edit these files.** The compiler owns them.
- **Never read them eagerly.** Treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## What is loaded at session start

`~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

## Rules

- Never exceed Tier B caps. Consolidate first.
- Always dedup before adding.
- For Tier A, the slug is the current cwd with `/` and `.` replaced by `-` (so `~` → `-Users-kristinarash`, `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV`, `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`). The harness injects the correct slug each session — use that, don't reconstruct it.
- **Write only to the current machine's slug.** Both machines are active as of 2026-09-10: Mac slugs are `-Users-kristinarash-*`, Windows slugs are `C--Users-eric-rash-*`. Analysis repo: `~/Desktop/DEV/Tech_Inventory_Analysis` — **a git repo** (erash11,
private). Supersedes the Mac-slug note of the same name, which still says "not a
git repo" and has the 08-29 baseline.

**Baseline 2026-09-15** (branch `refresh-2026-09-15`, not yet merged): 51
responses, 31 of 32 units answering for themselves, **Volleyball covered only by a
Business Office entry**, 185 products, 75 athlete-data candidates, 9 retirements.
Write-up `docs/FINDINGS_2026-09-15.md`; deliverables dated 2026-09-15.

**Getting the data.** Live survey is Microsoft Forms. The Forms page's download
menu sits in an iframe the browser tool cannot click; Eric downloaded the
OneDrive-synced workbook `Athletics Technology - Quick Inventory.xlsx` himself.

**Trap — renumbered IDs.** That synced workbook heads the column `Id`, has no
`Last modified time`, and renumbers responses (StatCrew went 5 → 3). Match
responses across exports on start + completion time; compare products on
unit × product, never by diffing `clean/`.

**Trap — Business Office proxies.** One Business Office respondent entered vendor
lists for 11 units (2 in August, 9 on 9/14) plus a department-wide contract list.
`clean_inventory.py` tags these `source=business-office`; coverage status
`BUSINESS OFFICE ONLY` marks a unit whose own staff never answered.

**Refresh:** save as `raw/Quick_Inventory_export_YYYY-MM-DD.xlsx`, run
`clean_inventory.py`, loop `unmapped_review.csv` into `aliases.py`, then the three
builders (`build_docx.py`, `build_exec_summary.py`, `build_tech_lists.py`) — they run
on Windows via Word COM. Update `PREVIOUS` in `build_docx.py` each run.

**Why:** the ID renumbering makes a naive diff report every row as changed, and the
proxy entries would otherwise read as 100% coverage.

**How to apply:** before the post-9/29 final run, merge the refresh branch first.
Related: [[ath-tech-framework]], [[baylor-house-style]].

- **Business Office-only products: 20 or 10?** The Executive Summary says 20. About 10 are vendors the Business Office listed for sport units that the units themselves didn't name. entries.description:
Exit a worktree session created by EnterWorktree and return the session to the original working directory.

## Scope

This tool ONLY operates on worktrees created by EnterWorktree in this session. It will NOT touch:
- Worktrees you created manually with `git worktree add`
- Worktrees from a previous session (even if created by EnterWorktree then)
- The directory you're in if EnterWorktree was never called

If called outside an EnterWorktree session, the tool is a **no-op**: it reports that no worktree session is active and takes no action. Filesystem state is unchanged.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly asks to "exit the worktree", "leave the worktree", "go back", or otherwise end the worktree session
- Do NOT call this proactively — only when the user asks

## Parameters

- `action` (required): `"keep"` or `"remove"`
  - `"keep"` — leave the worktree directory and branch intact on disk. Use this if the user wants to come back to the work later, or if there are changes to preserve.
  - `"remove"` — delete the worktree directory and its branch. Use this for a clean exit when the work is done or abandoned.
- `discard_changes` (optional, default false): only meaningful with `action: "remove"`. If the worktree has uncommitted files or commits not on the original branch, the tool will REFUSE to remove it unless this is set to `true`. If the tool returns an error listing changes, confirm with the user before re-invoking with `discard_changes: true`.

## Behavior

- Restores the session's working directory to where it was before EnterWorktree
- Clears CWD-dependent caches (system prompt sections, memory files, plans directory) so the session state reflects the original directory
- If a tmux session was attached to the worktree: killed on `remove`, left running on `keep` (its name is returned so the user can reattach)
- Once exited, EnterWorktree can be called again to create a fresh worktree

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). It copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/`, which is on the index list. One line of output; do this after Step 4 so today's STATUS is included.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.
- **Tier A does not cross machines — mirror it or lose it.** Project memory lives under a slug built from the project's absolute path, and that path differs on the Mac and the Windows laptop, so a Tier A file written today is not auto-injected tomorrow on the other machine. Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

**Always, in every repo touched (even for light sessions): update `docs/STATUS.md`.** It is the file the next session reads first, on either machine, in any harness. Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short:

- `## Current state` — two to five lines on where things stand today
- `## Next` — most important first
- `## Open questions` — decisions waiting on Eric
- `## Gotchas` — anything that will bite the next session

The dated handoff file is the detailed record; STATUS.md is the summary. Do Step 4 before the Step 2 commit so both land in the same push.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what>
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.
```

"Clear to sign off" means: every touched repo is pushed (or is a declared local-only repo). If anything is unpushed, the verdict is "Not clear" and the unpushed repo is the one thing blocking.

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

## Rules

- Push every touched DEV repo. Do not leave the laptop with unpushed work; the other machine pulls from GitHub, not from this disk.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.
- Total output should fit on one screen. The user is leaving; brevity is the deliverable.

# Handoff — 2026-09-15 — Technology inventory refresh

## What was worked on, and why

Eric downloaded a newer Microsoft Forms responses file for the Athletics
Technology Inventory. The job: pull it in, compare it with the previous run
(2026-08-29 export), and update the inventory reports. Done on the Baylor
Windows laptop; the refresh branch was merged to `main` (refresh commit
`baafe4a`, STATUS commit `7a6ed7d`).

## Result

- 51 submissions (up from 37). None of the 37 earlier responses changed.
- 31 of 32 units answered for themselves. **Volleyball's only entry is a
  Business Office vendor list** — its own staff have not answered.
- 185 products (+38), 75 athlete-data candidates, 120 single-unit, 9 retirements
  (new: Cizr, Constant Contact).
- Full write-up: `docs/FINDINGS_2026-09-15.md`.

## Decisions made, and the reasoning

1. **Business Office entries are tagged, not merged into unit responses.** One
   Business Office respondent entered 12 responses (Baseball 8/20, Football 8/28,
   ten on 9/14) — vendor lists from purchasing/contract records, plus the Business
   Office's own department-wide list. Counting them as unit responses would show
   100% coverage and hide that Volleyball never answered. `clean_inventory.py` sets
   `source = unit | business-office` for any response whose role is "Business
   Office"; coverage gets `unit_responses`, `business_office_entries`, and status
   `BUSINESS OFFICE ONLY`; `tech_master.csv` gets `unit_count_self_reported`.
2. **Responses are matched across exports on start + completion time, never ID.**
   The OneDrive-synced workbook renumbers IDs (StatCrew 5 → 3) and lacks "Last
   modified time". Documented in README.
3. **Executive summary follows Eric's 09-01 hand edit** (no eyebrow/meta block,
   In brief + numbers table + takeaways, no checklist). `SHOW_CHECKLIST = True`
   in `scripts/build_exec_summary.py` restores the checklist.
4. **Firstbeat stays "coming online".** The survey answer still says not in use;
   the 09-01 hand edit's "148 products" came from a duplicate Firstbeat line.
5. **Mapping calls** (all in `scripts/aliases.py`, 09-15 block): Notemeal →
   Teamworks; Teamworks Intelligence → Teamworks; Google Docs/Sheets/Forms/Calendar
   → Google Drive; "Influencer" → INFLCR; eVenue → Paciolan; FanMaker separate from
   Sidearm; Wilson/Head/Dunlop/fromuth excluded as equipment; Whistlestop **not**
   assumed to be Whistle.
6. **Builders made cross-platform** rather than Mac-only: `scripts/doc_platform.py`
   finds Baylor_Doc_Style on either machine and exports PDFs through Word (COM on
   Windows, AppleScript on Mac). Dates are now US style ("September 15, 2026").

## Files created or modified

Repo `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV\Tech_Inventory_Analysis`:
- `raw/Quick_Inventory_export_2026-09-15.xlsx` (new; has names/emails — repo is private)
- `scripts/doc_platform.py` (new), `scripts/build_tech_lists.py` (new)
- `scripts/clean_inventory.py`, `scripts/aliases.py`, `scripts/build_docx.py`,
  `scripts/build_exec_summary.py`
- `clean/coverage.csv`, `clean/tech_master.csv`, `clean/tech_inventory_long.csv`,
  `clean/stopped_using.csv`, `clean/unmapped_review.csv` (regenerated)
- `deliverables/Tech_Inventory_FINDINGS_ER_2026-09-15.{docx,pdf}` (7 pages)
- `deliverables/Tech_Inventory_EXEC_SUMMARY_ER_2026-09-15.{docx,pdf,html}` (1 page)
- `deliverables/Tech_Inventory_TECH_LISTS_ER_2026-09-15.{docx,pdf}` (4 pages)
- `docs/FINDINGS_2026-09-15.md` (new), `docs/STATUS.md`, `README.md`
- `docs/handoffs/2026-09-15-inventory-refresh.md` (this file)

Google Drive `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\05_SYSTEMS\SoftwareTechDocs\TechInventory_2026-08\`:
- the six 09-15 docx/pdf files (md5-identical to the repo copies)

Memory:
- `~/.claude/projects/C--Users-eric-rash-Desktop-DEV/memory/project_tech-inventory-refresh.md` (new) + index line
- `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (ATH Tech framework thread line)

## Next actions

1. Ask Volleyball for its own list before the 29 September deadline (the held-back
   Kenny/Jovon CC escalation now applies to one unit).
2. Eric to decide: the exec summary shows **20** Business Office-only products —
   about 10 are vendor lists for sport units, 10 are the Business Office's own
   department list. Keep 20, or report 10?
3. After 29 September: download the workbook, save to `raw/`, rerun the cleaner and
   the three builders; first update `PREVIOUS` in `scripts/build_docx.py` to the
   09-15 figures (51 / 31 / 185 / 75 / 120 / 9).
4. Confirm the mapping calls above; identify SCRL app, JABA, 135 - Tennis,
   DRVN.Golf, NeuroLogix, Whistlestop, Cizr.
5. Vendor data retention for the 9 retired products; detailed second-pass form on
   the 75 athlete-data candidates (Recovery Record first).

## Mid-flight / gotchas

- A leftover folder `.claude/worktrees/refresh-2026-09-15` could not be deleted
  (Windows "Permission denied" while a session held it). Everything in it is on
  `main`. Delete it later and run `git worktree prune`.
- The Mac-slug memory `project_tech-inventory-refresh.md` still has the 08-29
  baseline and says "not a git repo". Trust this repo's docs over it.
- The Forms "download responses" menu is inside an iframe the Chrome tool cannot
  click; the download has to be done by hand.
